title.raw: 卷114 志八十九 职官一

sentences.zh: 志八十九

translations.literal: Treatise Eighty-Nine
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 89

sentences.zh: 職官一

translations.literal: Official Posts One
translations.idiomatic: Official Posts, Part 1

sentences.zh: 太祖肇基東土，國俗淳壹，事簡職專，置八旗總管大臣、佐管大臣董統軍旅，置議政五大臣、理事十大臣釐治政刑，任用者止親貴數臣，官稱職立，人稱官置，興也勃焉。

translations.literal: When the Taizu founded his rule in the eastern lands, national customs were pure and uniform, affairs simple and offices specialized. He established Eight Banner grand marshals and assisting marshals to oversee the armies, and five deliberative ministers and ten administrative ministers to regulate government and punishments. Those appointed were only a few noble kinsmen; offices were titled according to duties, and men were placed according to offices—rise was vigorous indeed.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynastic founder laid the state’s foundations in the northeast, customs were plain and duties few. Grand and deputy commanders over the Eight Banners directed the armies; five deliberative ministers and ten administrative ministers handled government and law. Only a handful of kinsmen held office—titles matched tasks and men matched titles—and the rise was swift.

sentences.zh: 太宗厲精為治，設三館，置八承政，論功料勤，翕斯郅治。

translations.literal: The Taizong devoted himself diligently to governance, established three halls, appointed eight cheng-political directors, assessed merit and measured diligence, and thereby achieved supreme good order.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong threw himself into governance, founded three secretariats, appointed eight cheng-political directors, weighed merit and diligence, and brought the realm to high order.

sentences.zh: 世祖入關，因明遺制，內自閣、部以迄庶司，損益有物。

translations.literal: When the Shizu entered the Pass, he followed the Ming legacy system; from the inner Grand Secretariat and ministries down to the various offices, additions and reductions had substance.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shizu crossed into China proper, he adapted the Ming institutional legacy, adjusting the Grand Secretariat, ministries, and subordinate agencies with deliberate care.

sentences.zh: 籓部創建，名並七卿，外台督撫，杜其紛更，著為令甲。

translations.literal: The frontier departments were newly created, their names ranked with the seven ministries; provincial governors-general and governors were barred from frequent reshuffling, and this was written into binding statutes.
translations.idiomatic: New frontier ministries were established on a par with the seven chief ministries; governors-general and governors in the provinces were shielded from constant turnover, and these rules were codified as permanent law.

sentences.zh: 綠營提鎮以下，悉易差遣為官，旗營御前領衛，年宿位重，意任隆密。

translations.literal: Below the Green Standard Army commanders and regional commanders, all temporary assignments were changed to regular posts; for the Banner camps, the imperial bodyguard leaders held posts of long tenure and heavy rank, with trust intimate and weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Green Standard posts from regional commander downward were converted from temporary assignments to regular offices; Banner guards before the throne held posts of long standing and high rank, entrusted with intimate and weighty duties.

sentences.zh: 都統旗長，軍民合治，職視專圻駐防，分翰外畿，規撫京制。

translations.literal: Banner generals and company captains governed military and civilian affairs together; their duties resembled garrison command in exclusive jurisdictions, extending oversight beyond the capital region while regulating according to metropolitan norms.
translations.idiomatic: Banner generals and company captains administered both troops and civilians, much like garrison commanders in fixed territories, extending control beyond the capital while conforming to metropolitan regulations.

sentences.zh: 西北邊陲，守以重臣，綏靖蒙、番，方軌都護，斯皆因俗而治，得其宜已。

translations.literal: On the northwest frontier, heavy ministers were stationed as guards; they pacified Mongols and Tibetans, aligning with the model of frontier protectors—all these governed according to local custom and attained what was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The northwest marches were held by senior ministers who pacified Mongols and Tibetans along lines reminiscent of Han frontier protectors—each arrangement suited local custom and proved appropriate.

sentences.zh: 世宗綜覈，罷尚寶、行人、僉都諸目。

translations.literal: The Shizong conducted comprehensive review and abolished the posts of Court of Imperial Seals, Courier, and Assistant Censor-in-Chief, among others.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yongzheng reviewed the bureaucracy and eliminated such offices as the Court of Imperial Seals, the Courier Service, and assistant censor-in-chief posts.

sentences.zh: 高宗明哲，損參政、參議、副使、僉事諸銜，沙汰虛冗，奉職肅然。

translations.literal: The Gaozong was wise and perspicacious; he reduced the titles of Administrative Vice Commissioner, Administrative Commissioner, Vice Commissioner, and Assistant Commissioner, sifted out empty redundancy, and service became solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qianlong, clear-sighted in governance, trimmed vice-commissioner and assistant titles, purged hollow posts, and made official conduct notably disciplined.

sentences.zh: 嘉、道以降，整釐如舊。

translations.literal: From the Jiaqing and Daoguang reigns onward, rectification continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jiaqing and Daoguang periods onward, institutional tidying continued along established lines.

sentences.zh: 日久頹弛，精意浸失，日革月易，百職相侵。

translations.literal: As days lengthened, decline and laxity set in; refined intent gradually faded; daily reforms and monthly changes led the hundred offices to encroach on one another.
translations.idiomatic: Over time institutions slackened, careful purpose eroded, and constant tinkering left the hundred offices treading on one another’s duties.

sentences.zh: 光緒變法，宣統議制，品目張皇，掌寄紛雜，將以靖國，不益囂乎！

translations.literal: Under Guangxu’s reforms and Xuantong’s constitutional deliberations, ranks and categories multiplied extravagantly and responsibilities became tangled—intended to settle the state, did they not only add to the uproar!
translations.idiomatic: Guangxu’s reforms and Xuantong’s constitutional experiments multiplied ranks and muddled responsibilities—meant to steady the realm, they only deepened the clamor.

sentences.zh: 夫一國事權，操自樞垣，匯於六曹，分寄於疆吏。

translations.literal: As for a state’s governing authority, it was wielded from the privy council, gathered in the six ministries, and delegated to frontier officials.
translations.idiomatic: National authority issued from the privy council, pooled in the six ministries, and was delegated to provincial governors.

sentences.zh: 自改內三院為內閣，台輔拱袂。

translations.literal: After the inner three academies were changed to the Grand Secretariat, the chief ministers folded their sleeves in deference.
translations.idiomatic: Once the inner three academies became the Grand Secretariat, chief ministers stood largely idle.

sentences.zh: 迨軍機設，題本廢，內閣益類閒曹，六部長官數四，各無專事。

translations.literal: When the Grand Council was established and memorials on routine business were abolished, the Grand Secretariat increasingly resembled an idle office; heads of the six ministries numbered three or four each, with none holding exclusive duties.
translations.idiomatic: After the Grand Council was created and routine memorials discontinued, the Grand Secretariat became a largely ceremonial body; each ministry had several chiefs, none with a fixed portfolio.

sentences.zh: 甚或朝握銓衡，夕兼支計，甫主戎政，復領容台，一職數官，一官數職，曲存稟仰，建樹寧論。

translations.literal: Some held the power of appointments in the morning and concurrently managed expenditures in the evening; having just directed military affairs, they again headed the ceremonial office—one post with several officials, one official with several posts; bending to receive orders, what achievement could be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Some held the personnel power in the morning and the treasury at night, directed the army one day and the ceremonial office the next—posts multiplied on men and men on posts, all bent on awaiting orders rather than building policy.

sentences.zh: 時軍機之權，獨峙於其上，國家興大兵役，特簡經略大臣、參贊大臣，親寄軍要。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Council’s authority alone towered above; when the state undertook great military campaigns, special selection was made of frontier commissioners and assisting commissioners, with military essentials entrusted to them personally.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Council alone stood supreme; in major wars the throne specially appointed frontier commissioners and deputies and entrusted them with military affairs.

sentences.zh: 吏部助之用人，戶部協以巨饟，用能藉此雄職，奏厥膚功。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel assisted in selecting men; the Ministry of Revenue coordinated vast provisions—thus they could rely on these powerful posts to achieve meritorious results.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel supplied men and the Ministry of Revenue vast funds, enabling these powerful offices to win real victories.

sentences.zh: 自是權復移於經略，督撫儀品雖與相埒，然不過承號令、備策應而已。

translations.literal: Thereafter power shifted again to the frontier commissioners; governors-general and governors, though their ceremonial rank equaled that of grand secretaries, were no more than receivers of orders and providers of plans.
translations.idiomatic: Power then shifted to frontier commissioners; governors-general and governors matched grand secretaries in rank but merely carried orders and furnished plans.

sentences.zh: 厥後海疆釁起，經略才望稍爽，權力漸微。

translations.literal: Afterward, when troubles arose on the maritime frontier, the frontier commissioners’ talent and prestige declined somewhat, and their power gradually weakened.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as coastal crises erupted, frontier commissioners lost stature and their authority waned.

sentences.zh: 粵難糾紛，首相督師，屢僨厥事。

translations.literal: During the turmoil in Guangdong, the chief minister directed the army and repeatedly failed in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangdong crisis the chief minister took command and failed repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 朝廷間用督撫董戎，多不辱命，猶復不制以文法，故能霈施魄力，自是權又移於督撫。

translations.literal: The court occasionally employed governors-general and governors to direct military affairs; most did not dishonor their commissions, and moreover were not constrained by formal regulations—thus they could deploy bold energy, and from this power shifted again to governors-general and governors.
translations.idiomatic: The court then turned to governors-general and governors for military leadership; most succeeded, and because they were not hemmed in by routine law they could act boldly—so power passed again to the provinces.

sentences.zh: 同治中興，光緒還都，皆其力也。

translations.literal: The Tongzhi restoration and Guangxu’s return of the capital were all due to their strength.
translations.idiomatic: The Tongzhi revival and Guangxu’s restoration of the capital owed much to their efforts.

sentences.zh: 洎乎末造，親貴用事，權削四旁，厚集中央，疆事遂致不支焉。

translations.literal: By the dynasty’s last phase, imperial kinsmen held power; authority was stripped from the four sides and thickly gathered at the center, and frontier affairs thus became unsustainable.
translations.idiomatic: In the final years kinsmen dominated court politics, power was stripped from the provinces and hoarded at the center, and frontier administration collapsed under the strain.

sentences.zh: 初制內外群僚，滿、漢參用，蒙古、漢軍，次第分佈。

translations.literal: In the initial system for inner and outer officials, Manchus and Han were used together; Mongols and Han Bannermen were distributed in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: At first inner and outer posts mixed Manchus and Han, with Mongols and Han Bannermen gradually filling ranks as well.

sentences.zh: 康、雍兩朝，西北督撫，權定滿缺，領隊、辦事大臣，專任滿員，累朝膺閫外重寄者，滿臣為多。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi and Yongzheng reigns, northwest governors-general and governors were fixed as Manchu posts; brigade and administrative commissioners were exclusively Manchu appointments; across successive reigns those entrusted with heavy frontier duties were mostly Manchu officials.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi and Yongzheng northwest governors were reserved for Manchus, frontier commissioners were Manchu-only, and most holders of major field commands were Manchus.

sentences.zh: 逮文宗兼用漢人，勳業遂著。

translations.literal: When the Wenzong also employed Han Chinese, meritorious achievements then became notable.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Xianfeng emperor employed Han officials as well, distinguished service followed.

sentences.zh: 大抵中葉以前，開疆拓宇，功多成於滿人。

translations.literal: Generally, before the mid-dynasty, in opening territory and expanding domains, achievements were mostly accomplished by Manchus.
translations.idiomatic: Before the mid-dynasty, conquest and expansion owed most to Manchu commanders.

sentences.zh: 中葉以後，撥劇整亂，功多成於漢人。

translations.literal: After the mid-dynasty, in handling acute crises and restoring order, achievements were mostly accomplished by Han Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: After the mid-dynasty, crisis management and pacification owed most to Han officials.

sentences.zh: 季世釐定官制，始未嘗不欲混齊畛域，以固厥根本也。

translations.literal: In the final age when the official system was fixed, at first they had never not wished to blend and equalize boundaries in order to solidify the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Late reforms to the bureaucracy initially aimed to erase ethnic boundaries and strengthen the dynasty’s foundations.

sentences.zh: 而弊風相仍，一物自為鴻乙，徒致疑駴，雖危亡之政，無關典要，亦必輯而列之，以著一時故實，治亂之跡，庶皎然若覽焉。

translations.literal: Yet corrupt practices continued in succession; one thing became its own separate category, only causing doubt and alarm. Even policies of peril and ruin, though unrelated to essential institutions, must also be compiled and listed to record the facts of the time, so that the traces of order and disorder may be as clear as if viewed directly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet abuses persisted and categories multiplied until confusion reigned. Even doomed experiments unrelated to core institutions are recorded here so that the facts of the age—and the arc from order to chaos—may stand plain for the reader.

sentences.zh: 宗人府師傅保內閣稽查欽奉上諭事件處中書科軍機處內繙書房方略館

translations.literal: Court of the Imperial Clan; tutors and guardians; Grand Secretariat; Office for Scrutinizing Imperial Edicts; Secretariat of the Palace Secretariat; Grand Council; Inner Translation Office; Bureau for Military Plans
translations.idiomatic: Court of the Imperial Clan; tutors and guardians; Grand Secretariat; office for scrutinizing imperial edicts; Secretariat of the Palace Secretariat; Grand Council; Inner Translation Office; Bureau for Military Plans

sentences.zh: 吏部戶部三庫倉場關稅各差禮部會同四譯館樂部兵部刑部工部火藥局河道溝渠盛京五部

translations.literal: Ministry of Personnel; Ministry of Revenue; three treasuries; granary depots; customs duties and various assignments; Ministry of Rites; joint office with the Four Translation Bureaus; Music Office; Ministry of War; Ministry of Justice; Ministry of Works; Gunpowder Bureau; waterways; ditches and canals; five ministries at Mukden
translations.idiomatic: Ministry of Personnel; Ministry of Revenue; the three treasuries; granary depots; customs and related assignments; Ministry of Rites; joint office with the Four Translation Bureaus; Music Office; Ministry of War; Ministry of Justice; Ministry of Works; Gunpowder Bureau; waterways; ditches and canals; the five Mukden ministries

sentences.zh: 宗令，左、右宗正，左、右宗人，俱各一人。

translations.literal: Clan commander, left and right clan rectifiers, left and right clan administrators—one each.
translations.idiomatic: There was one clan commander, one left and one right clan rectifier, and one left and one right clan administrator.

sentences.zh: 宗室王、公爲之。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen of princely and ducal rank held these posts.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen of princely and ducal rank held these posts.

sentences.zh: 府丞，漢一人。

translations.literal: Vice director of the court—one Han Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: One Han vice director of the court.

sentences.zh: 正三品。

translations.literal: Rank: regular third grade.
translations.idiomatic: Rank: regular third grade.

sentences.zh: 其屬：堂主事，漢主事，經歷司經歷，並正六品。

translations.literal: Subordinates: secretariat clerk, Han secretariat clerk, registrar of the registry office—all regular sixth grade.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates included secretariat clerks, Han secretariat clerks, and registry registrars—all regular sixth grade.

sentences.zh: 左、右二司理事官，正五品。

translations.literal: Left and right bureau administrative officers—regular fifth grade.
translations.idiomatic: Left and right bureau administrative officers—regular fifth grade.

sentences.zh: 副理事官，從五品。

translations.literal: Deputy administrative officers—subordinate fifth grade.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy administrative officers—subordinate fifth grade.

sentences.zh: 主事，委署主事，俱各二人；

translations.literal: Directors and acting directors—two each.
translations.idiomatic: Directors and acting directors—two each.

sentences.zh: 筆帖式，效力筆帖式，各二十有四人。

translations.literal: Clerks and probationary clerks—twenty-four each.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks and probationary clerks—twenty-four each.

sentences.zh: 俱宗室爲之。

translations.literal: All were filled by imperial clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: All were filled by imperial clansmen.

sentences.zh: 宗令掌皇族屬籍，顯祖宣皇帝本支爲宗室，繫金黃帶。

translations.literal: The clan commander managed the imperial clan registers. The line of the Xianzu, Emperor Xuan, constituted the imperial clan and wore golden-yellow belts.
translations.idiomatic: The clan commander kept the imperial clan registers. Descendants of Emperor Xuan of the Xianzu line were registered as imperial clansmen and wore golden-yellow belts.

sentences.zh: 旁支曰覺羅，繫紅帶。

translations.literal: Collateral lines were called gioro and wore red belts.
translations.idiomatic: Collateral lines were called gioro and wore red belts.

sentences.zh: 革字者，繫紫帶。

translations.literal: Those stripped of their clan character wore purple belts.
translations.idiomatic: Those stripped of their clan character wore purple belts.

sentences.zh: 以時修輯玉牒，奠昭穆，序爵祿，宗室封爵十有二：曰和碩親王，曰多羅郡王，曰多羅貝勒，曰固山貝子，曰奉恩鎭國公，曰奉恩輔國公，曰不入八分鎭國公，曰不入八分輔國公，曰鎭國將軍，曰輔國將軍，曰奉國將軍，曰奉恩將軍。

translations.literal: He periodically compiled the imperial genealogy, fixed senior and junior lines, and ordered ranks and stipends. There were twelve noble ranks for the imperial clan: Prince of the First Rank, Prince of the Second Rank, Prince of the Third Rank, Prince of the Fourth Rank, Duke Who Pacifies the State by Grace, Duke Who Assists the State by Grace, Duke Who Pacifies the State Not Receiving the Eight Privileges, Duke Who Assists the State Not Receiving the Eight Privileges, General Who Pacifies the State, General Who Assists the State, General Who Serves the State, and General by Grace.
translations.idiomatic: He periodically revised the imperial genealogy, arranged senior and junior lines, and ordered ranks and stipends. Twelve ranks applied to the clan: Prince of the First Rank, Prince of the Second Rank, Prince of the Third Rank, Prince of the Fourth Rank, dukes pacifying or assisting the state by grace, dukes without the eight privileges, and the four grades of banner general.

sentences.zh: 嫡子受封者二等：曰世子，曰長子。

translations.literal: Heirs who received enfeoffment had two grades: heir apparent and eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffed legitimate sons held two titles: heir apparent and eldest son.

sentences.zh: 福晉、夫人之號，各視夫爵以爲差。

translations.literal: The titles of primary consort and lady each followed the husband’s rank in gradation.
translations.idiomatic: Titles for primary consorts and ladies varied according to their husbands’ ranks.

sentences.zh: 公主之等二：曰固倫公主，曰和碩公主。

translations.literal: Princesses had two grades: Princess of the First Rank and Princess of the Second Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial daughters held two princessly ranks: Princess of the First Rank and Princess of the Second Rank.

sentences.zh: 格格之等五：曰郡主，曰縣主，曰郡君，曰縣君，曰鄉君。

translations.literal: There were five grades of gege: commandery mistress, county mistress, commandery lady, county lady, and township lady.
translations.idiomatic: Five grades of clan daughters were recognized: commandery mistress, county mistress, commandery lady, county lady, and township lady.

sentences.zh: 不入五等曰宗女。

translations.literal: Those not entering the five grades were called clan daughters.
translations.idiomatic: Daughters outside the five grades were called clan daughters.

sentences.zh: 額駙品級，各視公主、格格等級以爲差。

translations.literal: The ranks of imperial sons-in-law each followed the princess or gege grade in gradation.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial sons-in-law received ranks matching those of their princess or gege wives.

sentences.zh: 麗派別，申敎誡，議賞罰，承陵廟祀事。

translations.literal: He clarified branch distinctions, conveyed admonitions, deliberated rewards and punishments, and undertook ancestral temple sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He clarified lineages, conveyed admonitions, deliberated rewards and punishments, and supervised ancestral temple rites.

sentences.zh: 宗正、宗人佐之。

translations.literal: The clan rectifiers and clan administrators assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Clan rectifiers and administrators assisted him.

sentences.zh: 府丞掌校漢文册籍。

translations.literal: The vice director managed collation of Chinese-language registers.
translations.idiomatic: The vice director collated Chinese-language registers.

sentences.zh: 左、右二司分掌左、右翼宗室、覺羅譜牒，序錄子女嫡庶、生卒、婚嫁，官爵、名謚；

translations.literal: The left and right bureaus respectively managed the genealogical records of left- and right-wing clansmen and gioro, recording in order children’s legitimacy, births and deaths, marriages, offices and ranks, and posthumous names;
translations.idiomatic: The left and right bureaus kept genealogies for the left and right wings, recording legitimacy, births and deaths, marriages, offices, and posthumous names;

sentences.zh: 並覈承襲次序，秩俸等差，及養給優卹諸事。

translations.literal: and also verified succession order, gradations of rank and stipend, and matters of maintenance, relief, and preferential condolence.
translations.idiomatic: and verified succession order, stipend grades, maintenance, relief, and condolence benefits.

sentences.zh: 堂主事掌清文奏稿。

translations.literal: Secretariat clerks managed Manchu memorial drafts.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat clerks drafted Manchu memorials.

sentences.zh: 漢主事掌漢文典籍。

translations.literal: Han secretariat clerks managed Chinese-language archives.
translations.idiomatic: Han secretariat clerks managed Chinese archives.

sentences.zh: 經歷掌出納文移。

translations.literal: Registrars managed dispatch and receipt of documents.
translations.idiomatic: Registrars handled incoming and outgoing documents.

sentences.zh: 筆帖式掌繙譯文書。

translations.literal: Clerks managed translation of documents.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks translated documents.

sentences.zh: 各部同。

translations.literal: The same applied in all ministries.
translations.idiomatic: The same applied in all ministries.

sentences.zh: 筆帖式爲滿員進身之階。

translations.literal: The clerk post was the ladder by which Manchu personnel advanced.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk post was the usual entry rank for Manchu officials.

sentences.zh: 國初，大學士達海、額爾德尼、索尼諸人，並起家武臣，以諳練國書，特恩賜號「巴克什」，即後之筆帖式也。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state, Grand Secretaries Dahai, Erdeni, Sonin, and others all rose from military posts; because they were skilled in the national script, they were specially granted the title “Bakshi”—that is, the later clerk post.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty’s founding Grand Secretaries Dahai, Erdeni, and Sonin rose from military careers; skilled in the Manchu script, they received the honorific “Bakshi”—the origin of the later clerk post.

sentences.zh: 厥後各署候補者紛不可紀矣。

translations.literal: Afterward candidates awaiting appointment in each office became too numerous to record.
translations.idiomatic: Later each agency swarmed with clerk candidates beyond count.

sentences.zh: 其兼領者：左、右翼宗學，總理學務王二人，稽察京堂官三人，並請旨簡派。

translations.literal: Offices concurrently held: left and right wing clan schools; two princes supervising academic affairs; three officials inspecting capital bureau chiefs—all appointed by imperial selection.
translations.idiomatic: Concurrent offices included the left and right clan schools; two princes supervising academic affairs; and three inspectors of capital bureau chiefs—all appointed by imperial selection.

sentences.zh: 總管四人，食七品俸。

translations.literal: Four superintendents, receiving seventh-grade stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Four superintendents on seventh-grade stipends.

sentences.zh: 副管十有六人，食八品俸。

translations.literal: Sixteen deputy superintendents, receiving eighth-grade stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen deputy superintendents on eighth-grade stipends.

sentences.zh: 並以宗室中分尊年長者引見補授。

translations.literal: All were presented and appointed from among senior clansmen by relative rank and age.
translations.idiomatic: All were presented and appointed from senior clansmen by rank and age.

sentences.zh: 清書敎習、騎射敎習各六人，漢書敎習八人。

translations.literal: Six Manchu-script instructors and six riding-and-archery instructors each; eight Chinese-script instructors.
translations.idiomatic: Six Manchu instructors, six riding-and-archery instructors, and eight Chinese instructors.

sentences.zh: 所轄銀庫，以本府堂官及滿洲大臣各一人領之，請旨簡派。

translations.literal: The silver treasury under its jurisdiction was led by one bureau chief of this court and one Manchu minister each, appointed by imperial selection.
translations.idiomatic: Its silver treasury was led by one court bureau chief and one Manchu minister, both appointed by imperial selection.

sentences.zh: 司官二人，由府引見補授。

translations.literal: Two bureau officers, presented by the court for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Two bureau officers appointed after presentation by the court.

sentences.zh: 筆帖式四人。

translations.literal: Four clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Four clerks.

sentences.zh: 空房，司官、筆帖式亦如之。

translations.literal: Vacant quarters: bureau officers and clerks likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Vacant quarters had the same bureau officers and clerks.

sentences.zh: 黃檔房，司官、筆帖式無員限。

translations.literal: Yellow archive office: no fixed quota for bureau officers and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The yellow archive office had no fixed quota for officers or clerks.

sentences.zh: 初制，列署篤恭殿前，置八和碩貝勒共議國政，各置官屬。

translations.literal: In the initial system, offices were arrayed before the Hall of Sincere Respect; eight princes of the first rank jointly deliberated state affairs, each with his own staff.
translations.idiomatic: Initially offices stood before the Hall of Sincere Respect, where eight first-rank princes jointly deliberated state affairs, each with his own staff.

sentences.zh: 順治九年，設宗人府，置宗令一人，親王、郡王爲之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shunzhi, the Court of the Imperial Clan was established with one clan commander—filled by princes of the first and second ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 9 the Court of the Imperial Clan was established with one clan commander—filled by first- and second-rank princes.

sentences.zh: 左、右宗正，貝勒、貝子兼攝。

translations.literal: Left and right clan rectifiers—held concurrently by third- and fourth-rank princes.
translations.idiomatic: Left and right clan rectifiers were held concurrently by third- and fourth-rank princes.

sentences.zh: 宗人，鎭國公、輔國公及將軍兼攝。

translations.literal: Clan administrators—held concurrently by dukes who pacify or assist the state and by banner generals.
translations.idiomatic: Clan administrators were held concurrently by state dukes and banner generals.

sentences.zh: 後擇賢，不以爵限。

translations.literal: Later the worthy were selected without limit by noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Later appointees were chosen for merit, not rank alone.

sentences.zh: 俱各二人。

translations.literal: Two each.
translations.idiomatic: Two each.

sentences.zh: 啓心郎，覺羅一人，漢軍二人，初制，秩視理事官。

translations.literal: Heart-opening counselors: one gioro, two Han Bannermen. In the initial system their rank equaled administrative officers.
translations.idiomatic: Heart-opening counselors: one gioro and two Han Bannermen. Initially their rank equaled that of administrative officers.

sentences.zh: 九年，改視侍郎。

translations.literal: In the ninth year it was changed to equal vice ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the rank was raised to vice minister.

sentences.zh: 始以滿臣不諳漢語，議事令坐其中。

translations.literal: At first, because Manchu officials did not know Chinese, they were made to sit among them during deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Because Manchu officials did not know Chinese, counselors were seated among them during deliberations.

sentences.zh: 後多緣以爲奸，康熙十二年省。

translations.literal: Later many used the post as a pretext for misconduct; in the twelfth year of Kangxi it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Later many abused the post; it was abolished in Kangxi 12.

sentences.zh: 與府丞並爲正官。

translations.literal: Together with the vice director they constituted regular chief posts.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the vice director they ranked as chief posts.

sentences.zh: 其郎中六人，康熙三十八年省二人。

translations.literal: Its directors numbered six; in the thirty-eighth year of Kangxi two were cut.
translations.idiomatic: Six directors served the court; two posts were cut in Kangxi 38.

sentences.zh: 員外郎四人，主事三人，以覺羅爲之，嗣改覺羅、滿洲參用。

translations.literal: Four vice directors and three secretaries, filled by gioro; later changed to mixed gioro and Manchu appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Four vice directors and three secretaries were first gioro-only, later filled by gioro and Manchus together.

sentences.zh: 堂主事二人，經歷三人，宗室、滿洲二人，漢一人。

translations.literal: Two secretariat clerks and three registrars—two clansmen or Manchus and one Han.
translations.idiomatic: Two secretariat clerks and three registrars—two clansmen or Manchus and one Han.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十八年省漢缺。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Kangxi the Han post was cut.
translations.idiomatic: The Han registrar post was cut in Kangxi 38.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十九年改用宗室。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Qianlong it was changed to use imperial clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 29 the post was reserved for imperial clansmen.

sentences.zh: 筆帖式二十有四人。

translations.literal: Twenty-four clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four clerks.

sentences.zh: 後增減無恆。

translations.literal: Later increases and reductions had no fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: Later numbers fluctuated without fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 初爲他赤哈哈番、筆帖式哈番，尋改六、七、八品及無頂戴筆帖式。

translations.literal: At first they were taci hahasan and clerk hahasan; soon changed to sixth-, seventh-, and eighth-grade clerks and clerks without official caps.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks began as taci and clerk bannermen, then became sixth-, seventh-, and eighth-grade posts and uncapped clerks.

sentences.zh: 各部同。

translations.literal: The same in all ministries.
translations.idiomatic: The same in all ministries.

sentences.zh: 康熙十二年，省啓心郎，增滿洲主事一人，分隸左、右二司。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kangxi the heart-opening counselors were abolished and one Manchu secretary was added, assigned to the left and right bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 12 the counselors were abolished and one Manchu secretary was added to each of the left and right bureaus.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，增漢主事二人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, two Han secretaries were added.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 two Han secretaries were added.

sentences.zh: 用進士出身者。

translations.literal: Drawn from jinshi degree-holders.
translations.idiomatic: They were drawn from jinshi degree-holders.

sentences.zh: 明年，改郎中爲理事官，員外郎爲副理事官，並定爲宗室、滿洲參用。

translations.literal: The following year, directors were changed to administrative officers and vice directors to deputy administrative officers, fixed as mixed imperial clan and Manchu appointments.
translations.idiomatic: The next year directors became administrative officers and vice directors deputy administrative officers, with posts shared between clansmen and Manchus.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十九年，允府丞儲麟趾奏，始專用宗室人員。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Qianlong, upon memorial of Vice Director Chu Linzhi, imperial clansmen alone were used.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 29, on Vice Director Chu Linzhi’s memorial, posts were reserved for imperial clansmen only.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，增置委署主事四人。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year, four acting secretaries were added.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-third year four acting secretaries were added.

sentences.zh: 筆帖式改。

translations.literal: Promoted from clerk posts.
translations.idiomatic: They were promoted from clerk posts.

sentences.zh: 太師、太傅、太保為三公。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Protector were the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Protector formed the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 正一品。

translations.literal: Regular first grade.
translations.idiomatic: Regular first grade.

sentences.zh: 少師、少傅、少保為三孤。

translations.literal: Junior Preceptor, Junior Tutor, and Junior Protector were the Three Solitaries.
translations.idiomatic: The Junior Preceptor, Junior Tutor, and Junior Protector formed the Three Solitaries.

sentences.zh: 從一品。

translations.literal: Subordinate first grade.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate first grade.

sentences.zh: 太子太師、太子太傅、太子太保，從一品。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Protector—subordinate first grade.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince’s grand preceptor, tutor, and protector held subordinate first grade.

sentences.zh: 太子少師、太子少傅、太子少保，正二品。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Junior Preceptor, Junior Tutor, and Junior Protector—regular second grade.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince’s junior preceptor, tutor, and protector held regular second grade.

sentences.zh: 俱東宮大臣，無員限，無專授。

translations.literal: All were Eastern Palace ministers, without fixed quota and without exclusive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: All served as Eastern Palace ministers, with no fixed quota and no exclusive appointment.

sentences.zh: 初沿明制，大臣有授公、孤者。

translations.literal: At first following the Ming system, great ministers were granted duke or solitary titles.
translations.idiomatic: Initially following Ming practice, senior ministers could receive duke or solitary titles.

sentences.zh: 嗣定為兼官、加官及贈官。

translations.literal: Later it was fixed as concurrent posts, added titles, and posthumous grants.
translations.idiomatic: Later these became concurrent posts, honorific additions, and posthumous grants.

sentences.zh: 內閣大學士，滿、漢各二人。

translations.literal: Grand Secretariat grand secretaries—two Manchus and two Han each.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Secretariat had two Manchu and two Han grand secretaries.

sentences.zh: 初制，滿員一品，漢員二品。

translations.literal: In the initial system, Manchu posts were first grade, Han posts second grade.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Manchu grand secretaries were first grade and Han ones second grade.

sentences.zh: 順治十五年，改與漢同。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Shunzhi, Manchu posts were changed to match Han.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 15 Manchu ranks were equalized with Han.

sentences.zh: 雍正八年，並定正一品。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongzheng, all were fixed at regular first grade.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 8 all were fixed at regular first grade.

sentences.zh: 協辦大學士，滿、漢各一人。

translations.literal: Assistant grand secretaries—one Manchu and one Han each.
translations.idiomatic: There was one Manchu and one Han assistant grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 尚書內特簡。

translations.literal: Specially selected from among ministers.
translations.idiomatic: They were specially selected from serving ministers.

sentences.zh: 正一品。

translations.literal: Regular first grade.
translations.idiomatic: Regular first grade.

sentences.zh: 學士，滿洲六人，漢四人。

translations.literal: Chancellors—six Manchus and four Han.
translations.idiomatic: Six Manchu and four Han chancellors served the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初制，滿員二品，漢員三品。

translations.literal: In the initial system, Manchu posts were second grade, Han posts third grade.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Manchu chancellors were second grade and Han ones third grade.

sentences.zh: 順治十五年，並改正五品，兼禮部侍郎者正三品。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Shunzhi, all were changed to regular fifth grade; those also holding Ministry of Rites vice minister rank were regular third grade.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 15 all became regular fifth grade, while those also vice ministers of Rites were regular third grade.

sentences.zh: 雍正八年，定從二品。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongzheng, fixed at subordinate second grade.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 8 the rank was fixed at subordinate second grade.

sentences.zh: 後皆兼禮部侍郎銜。

translations.literal: Later all held concurrent Ministry of Rites vice minister titles.
translations.idiomatic: Later all held concurrent vice-minister of Rites titles.

sentences.zh: 典籍□典籍，滿、漢、漢軍各二人。

translations.literal: Archivists—two Manchus, two Han, and two Han Bannermen each.
translations.idiomatic: Two Manchu, two Han, and two Han Banner archivists served the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 正七品。

translations.literal: Regular seventh grade.
translations.idiomatic: Regular seventh grade.

sentences.zh: 侍讀學士，滿洲四人，蒙、漢各二人。

translations.literal: Reader-chancellors—four Manchus, two Mongols, and two Han.
translations.idiomatic: Four Manchu, two Mongol, and two Han reader-chancellors served the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初兼太常寺卿銜，尋罷。

translations.literal: At first they concurrently held Court of Imperial Sacrifices director titles; soon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: They initially held concurrent Court of Imperial Sacrifices director titles, soon dropped.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年，定從四品。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongzheng, fixed at subordinate fourth grade.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 3 the rank was fixed at subordinate fourth grade.

sentences.zh: 中書，正七品。

translations.literal: Secretaries—regular seventh grade.
translations.idiomatic: Secretaries held regular seventh grade.

sentences.zh: 滿洲七十人，蒙古十有六人，漢軍八人。

translations.literal: Seventy Manchus, sixteen Mongols, and eight Han Bannermen.
translations.idiomatic: There were seventy Manchu, sixteen Mongol, and eight Han Banner secretaries.

sentences.zh: 貼寫中書，滿洲四十人，蒙古六人。

translations.literal: Copying secretaries—forty Manchus and six Mongols.
translations.idiomatic: Forty Manchu and six Mongol copying secretaries served the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大學士掌鈞國政，贊詔命，釐憲典，議大禮、大政，裁酌可否入告。

translations.literal: Grand secretaries managed the balance of state affairs, assisted in edicts, rectified statutes, deliberated great rites and great policies, and weighed what might be reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Grand secretaries steered state policy, drafted edicts, refined statutes, debated major rites and policies, and advised the throne on what should be done.

sentences.zh: 協辦佐之。

translations.literal: Assistant grand secretaries aided them.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant grand secretaries supported them.

sentences.zh: 修實錄、史、志，充監修總裁官。

translations.literal: They compiled veritable records, histories, and gazetteers, serving as supervising chief editors.
translations.idiomatic: They oversaw compilation of veritable records, histories, and gazetteers as supervising editors-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 經筵領講官。

translations.literal: They led lecturers at the classics exposition.
translations.idiomatic: They led lecturers at the imperial classics exposition.

sentences.zh: 會試充考試官。

translations.literal: They served as metropolitan examination examiners.
translations.idiomatic: They served as chief examiners for the metropolitan examinations.

sentences.zh: 殿試充讀卷官。

translations.literal: They served as palace examination readers of papers.
translations.idiomatic: They read papers at the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 春秋釋奠，攝行祭事。

translations.literal: At spring and autumn sacrifices they performed rites by proxy.
translations.idiomatic: At spring and autumn Confucian sacrifices they officiated on the emperor’s behalf.

sentences.zh: 學士掌敷奏。

translations.literal: Chancellors managed presentation of memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors presented memorials to the throne.

sentences.zh: 侍讀學士掌典校。

translations.literal: Reader-chancellors managed collation of texts.
translations.idiomatic: Reader-chancellors collated texts.

sentences.zh: 侍讀掌勘對。

translations.literal: Readers managed checking and comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Readers checked and compared documents.

sentences.zh: 典籍掌出納文移。

translations.literal: Archivists managed dispatch and receipt of documents.
translations.idiomatic: Archivists handled incoming and outgoing documents.

sentences.zh: 內閣為典掌絲綸之地，自大學士以下，皆不置印，惟典籍置之，以鈐往來文牒。

translations.literal: The Grand Secretariat was the place that managed imperial silk edicts; from grand secretaries downward none held seals—only archivists held them, to stamp incoming and outgoing documents.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Secretariat managed imperial edicts; from grand secretaries down no one held a seal—only archivists did, to stamp official correspondence.

sentences.zh: 中書掌撰擬、繙譯。

translations.literal: Secretaries managed drafting and translation.
translations.idiomatic: Secretaries drafted and translated documents.

sentences.zh: 分辦本章處凡五：曰滿本房，漢本房，蒙古本房，滿簽票處，漢簽票處。

translations.literal: Offices for handling memorials numbered five in all: Manchu memorial office, Han memorial office, Mongol memorial office, Manchu endorsement office, and Han endorsement office.
translations.idiomatic: Five offices handled memorials: Manchu, Han, and Mongol memorial offices plus Manchu and Han endorsement offices.

sentences.zh: 又誥敕房，稽察房，收發紅本副本處，飯銀庫，俱由大學士委侍讀以下官司之。

translations.literal: Also the edict office, scrutiny office, office for receiving and dispatching red-copy duplicates, and meal-silver treasury—all administered by grand secretaries through readers and lower offices.
translations.idiomatic: The edict office, scrutiny office, red-copy dispatch office, and meal-silver treasury were all run by grand secretaries through readers and subordinate staff.

sentences.zh: 惟批本處額置滿洲翰林官一人，請旨簡派。

translations.literal: Only the endorsement office had a fixed quota of one Manchu Hanlin official, appointed by imperial selection.
translations.idiomatic: Only the endorsement office had one Manchu Hanlin post, filled by imperial appointment.

sentences.zh: 中書七人。

translations.literal: Seven secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Seven secretaries served there.

sentences.zh: 滿中書內補授。

translations.literal: Filled by promotion from among Manchu secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: They were promoted from among Manchu secretaries.

sentences.zh: 初，天聰二年，建文館，命儒臣分直。

translations.literal: At first, in the second year of Tiancong, a literary hall was built and Confucian officials were ordered to serve in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancong 2 a literary hall was established and Confucian officials were assigned in rotation.

sentences.zh: 十年，更名內三院。

translations.literal: In the tenth year it was renamed the Inner Three Academies.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year it became the Inner Three Academies.

sentences.zh: 曰國史，曰秘書，曰弘文。

translations.literal: They were called State History, Secretariat, and Hongwen.
translations.idiomatic: They were the State History, Secretariat, and Hongwen academies.

sentences.zh: 始亦沿承政名，後各置大學士一人。

translations.literal: At first they also followed the cheng-political title; later each was given one grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: They initially used cheng-political titles; later each academy received one grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，置滿、漢大學士，不備官，兼各部尚書銜。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, Manchu and Han grand secretaries were established, not filling full posts, concurrently holding ministry minister titles.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 Manchu and Han grand secretaries were appointed without full posts, concurrently holding ministry minister titles.

sentences.zh: 學士，滿洲，康熙九年改置二人，十年增四人，通舊為六人。

translations.literal: Chancellors—Manchu: in the ninth year of Kangxi changed to two posts, in the tenth year four added, totaling six with the old.
translations.idiomatic: Manchu chancellors were set at two in Kangxi 9 and raised to six in Kangxi 10.

sentences.zh: 漢軍，康熙十年改置二人，十二年並入漢缺。

translations.literal: Han Banner: in the tenth year of Kangxi changed to two posts; in the twelfth year merged into Han posts.
translations.idiomatic: Han Banner chancellors were set at two in Kangxi 10 and merged into Han posts in Kangxi 12.

sentences.zh: 各三人，漢學士無員限。

translations.literal: Three each; Han chancellors had no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Three each served; Han chancellors had no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 康熙十年改置二人，明年增二人，十二年省漢軍入漢缺，通舊為四人。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kangxi changed to two posts; the next year two added; in the twelfth year Han Banner posts cut and merged into Han posts, totaling four with the old.
translations.idiomatic: Han chancellors were set at two in Kangxi 10, raised to four in Kangxi 11, and Han Banner posts merged into Han posts in Kangxi 12.

sentences.zh: 典籍，滿、漢、漢軍各三人。

translations.literal: Archivists—three Manchus, three Han, and three Han Bannermen each.
translations.idiomatic: Three Manchu, three Han, and three Han Banner archivists served initially.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年改置二人。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi changed to two posts.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 9 the quota was reduced to two.

sentences.zh: 侍讀，滿洲十有一人，清文五人，清漢文六人。

translations.literal: Readers—eleven Manchus: five Manchu-script and six Manchu-Chinese-script.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven Manchu readers served: five for Manchu script and six for Manchu-Chinese script.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十八年省清文一人，清漢文二人。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Kangxi one Manchu-script and two Manchu-Chinese-script posts were cut.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 38 one Manchu-script and two Manchu-Chinese reader posts were cut.

sentences.zh: 尋復增二人，通舊為十人。

translations.literal: Soon two were added back, totaling ten with the old.
translations.idiomatic: Two posts were soon restored, bringing the total back to ten.

sentences.zh: 蒙古、漢軍、康熙九年各置二人。

translations.literal: Mongol and Han Banner: in the ninth year of Kangxi two each were established.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol and Han Banner readers were set at two each in Kangxi 9.

sentences.zh: 漢康熙九年省。

translations.literal: Han: cut in the ninth year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Han reader posts were cut in Kangxi 9.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年置二人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng two were established.
translations.idiomatic: Two Han reader posts were restored in Yongzheng 4.

sentences.zh: 各三人。

translations.literal: Three each.
translations.idiomatic: Three each served thereafter.

sentences.zh: 中書，滿洲七十有五人，蒙古十有九人，漢軍十有三人，漢三十有六人。

translations.literal: Secretaries—seventy-five Manchus, nineteen Mongols, thirteen Han Bannermen, and thirty-six Han.
translations.idiomatic: There were seventy-five Manchu, nineteen Mongol, thirteen Han Banner, and thirty-six Han secretaries.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十八年省滿洲、漢軍各五人，蒙古三人，漢四人。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Kangxi five Manchu and five Han Banner posts were cut, three Mongol, and four Han.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 38 five Manchu and five Han Banner secretary posts were cut, along with three Mongol and four Han posts.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十三年復省漢三人。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong three Han posts were again cut.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 13 three more Han secretary posts were cut.

sentences.zh: 二年，定為正二品衙門，以翰林官分隸之。

translations.literal: In the second year it was fixed as a regular second-grade office, with Hanlin officials assigned to it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year it was made a regular second-grade office staffed by Hanlin officials.

sentences.zh: 三院上並系「內翰林」字。

translations.literal: Above the three academies was added the designation “Inner Hanlin.”
translations.idiomatic: The three academies were collectively titled Inner Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 八年，置侍讀學士，滿、蒙、漢軍各三人。

translations.literal: In the eighth year reader-chancellors were established—three Manchus, three Mongols, and three Han Bannermen each.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year three Manchu, three Mongol, and three Han Banner reader-chancellors were appointed.

sentences.zh: 十八年增滿洲二人，蒙古三人。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year two Manchu and three Mongol posts were added.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year two Manchu and three Mongol reader-chancellor posts were added.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年增滿洲四人，餘改置二人。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi four Manchu posts were added; the rest were changed to two each.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 9 four Manchu reader-chancellor posts were added and other quotas were set at two.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十七年省漢軍入漢缺。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Qianlong Han Banner posts were cut and merged into Han posts.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 17 Han Banner reader-chancellor posts were merged into Han posts.

sentences.zh: 十年，置三院漢大學士各二人。

translations.literal: In the tenth year two Han grand secretaries were established for each of the three academies.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year each of the three academies received two Han grand secretaries.

sentences.zh: 十五年，更名內閣，別置翰林院官，以大學士分兼。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year it was renamed the Grand Secretariat; Hanlin posts were separately established, with grand secretaries holding them concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year it became the Grand Secretariat; Hanlin posts were separated and grand secretaries held them concurrently.

sentences.zh: 殿閣曰中和殿、保和殿、文華殿、武英殿、文淵閣、東閣，諸大學士仍兼尚書，學士亦如之。

translations.literal: Hall pavilions were called Hall of Central Harmony, Hall of Preserving Harmony, Hall of Literary Glory, Hall of Military Eminence, Pavilion of Literary Depth, and Eastern Pavilion; grand secretaries still concurrently held ministry posts, and chancellors likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Grand secretaries were attached to the halls of Central Harmony, Preserving Harmony, Literary Glory, Military Eminence, Literary Depth, and the Eastern Pavilion, still concurrently holding ministry posts as did chancellors.

sentences.zh: 十八年，復三院舊制。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the old three-academy system was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the three-academy system was restored.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年，仍別置翰林院，改三院為內閣，置滿、漢大學士四人。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi the Hanlin Academy was again separately established; the three academies were changed to the Grand Secretariat, with four Manchu and Han grand secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 9 the Hanlin Academy was re-established separately, the three academies became the Grand Secretariat, and four Manchu and Han grand secretaries were appointed.

sentences.zh: 雍正九年，禮部尚書陳元龍、左都御史尹泰特授額外大學士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongzheng, Minister of Rites Chen Yuanlong and Censor-in-Chief of the Left Yin Tai were specially granted extra grand secretary posts.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 9 Minister of Rites Chen Yuanlong and Left Censor-in-Chief Yin Tai were specially made extra grand secretaries.

sentences.zh: 置協辦自此始。

translations.literal: Establishment of assistant grand secretaries began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant grand secretaries date from this change.

sentences.zh: 厥後多至六人，少或一二人。

translations.literal: Afterward they numbered as many as six or as few as one or two.
translations.idiomatic: Later their number ranged from one or two to as many as six.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十三年，始定大學士、協辦大學士員限，省中和殿，增體仁閣，以三殿、三閣為定制，唯保和殿不常置。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong, quotas for grand secretaries and assistant grand secretaries were first fixed; the Hall of Central Harmony was cut and the Pavilion of Cherishing Benevolence added; three halls and three pavilions became the fixed system, only the Hall of Preserving Harmony not regularly established.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 13 quotas were fixed for grand and assistant grand secretaries; Central Harmony was dropped and Cherishing Benevolence added, making three halls and three pavilions standard—except Preserving Harmony, which was rarely filled.

sentences.zh: 嗣後授保和者止傅恆一人。

translations.literal: Afterward only Fu Heng alone was granted Preserving Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Only Fu Heng was ever granted the Preserving Harmony hall thereafter.

sentences.zh: 凡遇歲時慶節朝會，漢員列滿員下。

translations.literal: Whenever seasonal festivals and court assemblies occurred, Han officials were ranked below Manchu officials.
translations.idiomatic: At seasonal festivals and court assemblies Han officials stood below Manchu officials.

sentences.zh: 自光緒間李鴻章系文華殿銜，而寶鋆時系武英殿，班轉居其右。

translations.literal: From the Guangxu period Li Hongzhang held the Hall of Literary Glory title while Bao Jun held the Hall of Military Eminence; in court order Bao turned to stand to his right.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangxu period Li Hongzhang held Literary Glory while Bao Jun held Military Eminence, placing Bao to Li’s right in court order.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，停兼尚書銜。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year concurrent ministry minister titles were discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year concurrent ministry minister titles were discontinued.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，改組內閣，別令大學士序次翰林院。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong the Grand Secretariat was reorganized, and grand secretaries were separately ordered after the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 3 the Grand Secretariat was reorganized and grand secretaries ranked after the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 先是世祖親政，日至票本房，大學士司票擬，意任隆密。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Shizu personally governed, he daily went to the memorial drafting office; grand secretaries managed draft endorsements, with trust weighty and intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, under the Shizu’s personal rule, he visited the memorial drafting office daily; grand secretaries drafted endorsements and enjoyed intimate, weighty trust.

sentences.zh: 康熙時，改內閣，分其職設翰林院。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi period it was changed to the Grand Secretariat and its duties divided by establishing the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi it became the Grand Secretariat and the Hanlin Academy took over part of its duties.

sentences.zh: 雍正時，青海告警，復分其職設軍機處，議者謂與內三院無異。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng period, when Qinghai raised alarms, its duties were again divided by establishing the Grand Council; commentators said this differed little from the Inner Three Academies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongzheng, after alarms from Qinghai, the Grand Council was created to share its duties—commentators said this differed little from the Inner Three Academies.

sentences.zh: 顧南書房翰林雖典內廷書詔，而軍國機要綜歸內閣，猶為重寄。

translations.literal: Yet although Hanlin of the Southern Study managed inner-court edicts, military and state essentials still gathered in the Grand Secretariat—it remained a weighty trust.
translations.idiomatic: Although Southern Study Hanlin drafted inner-court edicts, military and state essentials still centered in the Grand Secretariat, which remained a weighty trust.

sentences.zh: 至本章歸內閣，大政由樞臣承旨，權任漸輕矣。

translations.literal: When routine memorials returned to the Grand Secretariat but great policy was carried out by privy councillors receiving imperial intent, authority and responsibility gradually lightened.
translations.idiomatic: Once routine memorials returned to the Grand Secretariat while great policy passed to privy councillors receiving imperial intent, its authority gradually faded.

sentences.zh: 稽察欽奉上諭事件處，兼理大臣無員限。

translations.literal: Office for scrutinizing matters of imperial edicts received with reverence; concurrently administering ministers had no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: The office that scrutinized reverently received imperial edict matters had no fixed quota for concurrently serving ministers.

sentences.zh: 滿、漢大學士、尚書、左都御史內特簡。

translations.literal: Specially selected from among Manchu and Han grand secretaries, ministers, and the left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: They were specially chosen from Manchu and Han grand secretaries, ministers, and the left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 掌察諸司諭旨特交事件，督以例限。

translations.literal: Managed scrutiny of specially assigned edict matters from all offices, supervising them according to statutory deadlines.
translations.idiomatic: It scrutinized specially assigned edict matters from all ministries and enforced statutory deadlines.

sentences.zh: 委署主事，滿洲一人。

translations.literal: One acting Manchu secretary.
translations.idiomatic: One acting Manchu secretary served there.

sentences.zh: 行走司官，漢四人。

translations.literal: Four Han bureau officials on rotating duty.
translations.idiomatic: Four Han bureau officials served in rotation.

sentences.zh: 並於吏、兵、刑、工四部選補。

translations.literal: All were selected and appointed from the Ministries of Personnel, War, Justice, and Works.
translations.idiomatic: They were drawn from the Personnel, War, Justice, and Works ministries.

sentences.zh: 筆帖式四十人。

translations.literal: Forty clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Forty clerks served the office.

sentences.zh: 額外筆帖式八人。

translations.literal: Eight extra clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Eight additional clerk posts were authorized.

sentences.zh: 中書科，稽察科事內閣學士，滿、漢各一人，由內閣學士內特簡。

translations.literal: The Secretariat Chancery: for scrutinizing chancery affairs, one Manchu and one Han Grand Secretariat chancellor each, specially selected from among secretariat chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: The edict chancery was overseen for scrutiny by one Manchu and one Han inner-court chancellor, each specially chosen from the secretariat chancellors.

sentences.zh: 掌稽頒冊軸。

translations.literal: Managed scrutiny and issuance of registers and scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: It scrutinized and issued registers and scrolls.

sentences.zh: 掌印中書，滿洲一人。

translations.literal: One Manchu seal-holding secretary.
translations.idiomatic: One Manchu secretary held the chancery seal.

sentences.zh: 掌科中書，漢一人。

translations.literal: One Han chancery-directing secretary.
translations.idiomatic: One Han secretary directed chancery affairs.

sentences.zh: 中書，並從七品。

translations.literal: Secretaries—all subordinate seventh grade.
translations.idiomatic: Secretaries all held subordinate seventh grade.

sentences.zh: 滿洲一人，漢三人，掌繕書誥敕。

translations.literal: One Manchu and three Han, managing copying of edicts and commissions.
translations.idiomatic: One Manchu and three Han secretaries copied edicts and commissions of appointment.

sentences.zh: 筆帖式十人。

translations.literal: Ten clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Ten clerks served the chancery.

sentences.zh: 初制，置滿洲中書舍人一人，乾隆十四年增一人。

translations.literal: In the initial system, one Manchu Secretariat secretary was established; in the fourteenth year of Qianlong one more was added.
translations.idiomatic: Initially one Manchu edict secretary was appointed; in Qianlong 14 a second was added.

sentences.zh: 漢中書舍人八人。

translations.literal: Eight Han Secretariat secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Eight Han edict secretaries served.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年派兼內閣行走。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng they were ordered also to serve in the Grand Secretariat in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 13 they were also assigned to rotate through the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十三年省四人。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong four posts were cut.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 13 four posts were abolished.

sentences.zh: 順治九年，置滿洲記事官，同掌科事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shunzhi, Manchu record-keeping officials were established, jointly managing chancery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 9 Manchu record-keepers were appointed to manage chancery affairs jointly.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年，改記事官為中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi, record-keeping officials were changed to Secretariat secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 9 record-keepers became edict secretaries.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十六年，置管中書科事漢內閣學士一人。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year of Qianlong, one Han Grand Secretariat chancellor was established to manage Secretariat Chancery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 36 one Han inner-court chancellor was appointed to oversee the edict chancery.

sentences.zh: 明年，改管科事為稽察科事；

translations.literal: The following year, managing chancery affairs was changed to scrutinizing chancery affairs;
translations.idiomatic: The next year oversight of chancery affairs became scrutiny of chancery affairs;

sentences.zh: 增置滿洲內閣學士一人；

translations.literal: one Manchu Grand Secretariat chancellor was added;
translations.idiomatic: one Manchu inner-court chancellor was added;

sentences.zh: 改中書舍人為中書科，置掌印中書，滿、漢各一人。

translations.literal: Secretariat secretaries were changed to the Secretariat Chancery, with seal-holding secretaries—one Manchu and one Han each.
translations.idiomatic: Edict secretaries became the edict chancery, with one Manchu and one Han seal-holding secretary each.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年省。

translations.literal: Cut in the third year of Xuantong.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished in Xuantong 3.

sentences.zh: 軍機處軍機大臣，無定員，由大學士、尚書、侍郎內特旨召入。

translations.literal: Grand Council grand councillors—no fixed quota; specially summoned by imperial rescript from among grand secretaries, ministers, and vice ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Grand councillors of the Grand Council had no fixed quota and were summoned by special imperial order from grand secretaries, ministers, and vice ministers.

sentences.zh: 區其名曰大臣，曰大臣上行走。

translations.literal: Their titles were distinguished as grand councillor and grand councillor senior attendant on duty.
translations.idiomatic: They were titled grand councillor or senior grand councillor on duty.

sentences.zh: 其初入者加「學習」二字。

translations.literal: Those first entering had the words “in training” added.
translations.idiomatic: New appointees were marked “in training.”

sentences.zh: 掌軍國大政，以贊機務。

translations.literal: Managed great military and state policy to assist in privy affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They directed major military and state policy and advised on privy council business.

sentences.zh: 常日侍直，應對獻替，巡幸亦如之。

translations.literal: Daily attended on duty, responding and offering advice; the same on imperial tours.
translations.idiomatic: They attended daily, answered the throne, and offered counsel—also on imperial tours.

sentences.zh: 明降諭旨，述交內閣。

translations.literal: Clearly transmitted descending edicts and handed them to the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: They drafted imperial edicts and passed them to the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 諭本處行者，封寄所司。

translations.literal: Where edicts were to be executed on the spot, they were sealed and sent to the relevant office.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts to be executed locally were sealed and sent to the responsible agency.

sentences.zh: 並冊藏存記人員，屆時題奏。

translations.literal: Also registered and stored personnel records, reporting to the throne at the proper time.
translations.idiomatic: They also kept registers of stored personnel and memorialized the throne when due.

sentences.zh: 其屬曰章京，滿洲十有六人，漢二十人，名曰行走，分頭班、二班。

translations.literal: Their subordinates were called zhangjing—sixteen Manchus and twenty Han, called “on duty,” divided into first and second shifts.
translations.idiomatic: Their staff were council clerks: sixteen Manchu and twenty Han, called duty officers, in first and second shifts.

sentences.zh: 初無定額，嘉慶四年定每班八人。

translations.literal: At first no fixed quota; in the fourth year of Jiaqing fixed at eight per shift.
translations.idiomatic: Initially there was no fixed quota; in Jiaqing 4 each shift was set at eight.

sentences.zh: 後增减無恆。

translations.literal: Later increases and decreases were not constant.
translations.idiomatic: Later the numbers changed without a fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 光緒三十二年定三十有六人，復定領班秩視三品，幫領班秩視四品，餘並以原官充補。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Guangxu fixed at thirty-six; also fixed shift leaders at third-grade rank, assistant shift leaders at fourth-grade rank, the rest all filling posts in their original ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 32 the quota was set at thirty-six; shift leaders ranked as third grade and assistants as fourth, while others kept their original ranks.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，改領班為從三品，幫領班為從四品。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, shift leaders were changed to subordinate third grade, assistant shift leaders to subordinate fourth grade.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year shift leaders became subordinate third grade and assistants subordinate fourth grade.

sentences.zh: 分掌清文、漢字。

translations.literal: Divided management of Manchu-script and Chinese-script documents.
translations.idiomatic: They handled Manchu and Chinese documents separately.

sentences.zh: 初設議政處，令鞏阿岱等為議政大臣，參畫軍要。

translations.literal: At first the Council of Deliberation was established, with Gonga Dai and others as deliberative ministers to plan military essentials.
translations.idiomatic: A Council of Deliberation was first set up, with Gonga Dai and others as deliberative ministers to plan military affairs.

sentences.zh: 雍正十年，用兵西北，慮儤直者洩機密，始設軍機房，後改軍機處，而滿洲大學士尚有兼議政銜者。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongzheng, with war in the northwest, fearing those on rotating duty might leak secrets, the Military Secrets Office was first established, later changed to the Grand Council; yet Manchu grand secretaries still held concurrent deliberative titles.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 10, with northwestern campaigns under way, fear of leaks from rotating duty officers led to a military secrets office, later the Grand Council—though some Manchu grand secretaries still held deliberative titles.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十六年停。

translations.literal: Discontinued in the fifty-sixth year of Qianlong.
translations.idiomatic: This practice ended in Qianlong 56.

sentences.zh: 高宗蒞政，更名總理處，尋復如初。

translations.literal: When the Gaozong assumed power, it was renamed the General Secretariat; soon restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gaozong took the throne it was renamed the General Secretariat, then soon restored.

sentences.zh: 時入直者皆重臣。

translations.literal: Those then attending on duty were all weighty ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Those on duty at the time were all senior statesmen.

sentences.zh: 故事，親王不假事權。

translations.literal: By precedent, princes were not granted operational authority.
translations.idiomatic: By custom princes were not given executive power.

sentences.zh: 至嘉慶四年，始命成親王入直，旋出之。

translations.literal: Not until the fourth year of Jiaqing was Prince Cheng ordered to attend on duty, soon removed.
translations.idiomatic: Not until Jiaqing 4 was Prince Cheng ordered on duty, then soon removed.

sentences.zh: 咸豐間，覆命恭親王入直，歷三朝領班如故。

translations.literal: In the Xianfeng period, Prince Gong was again ordered to attend on duty, leading shifts through three reigns as before.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianfeng, Prince Gong was again ordered on duty and led shifts through three reigns as before.

sentences.zh: 嗣是醇賢親王、禮親王、慶親王等踵相躡。

translations.literal: Thereafter Prince Chun the Worthy, Prince Li, Prince Qing, and others followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Princes Chun the Worthy, Li, Qing, and others followed one after another.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十七年，設政務處，以軍機大臣領督辦事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Guangxu, the Government Affairs Office was established, with grand councillors leading as supervising directors.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 27 a Government Affairs Office was set up, headed by grand councillors as supervising directors.

sentences.zh: 參預大臣無定員。

translations.literal: Participating ministers had no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Participating ministers had no fixed number.

sentences.zh: 提調、幫提調、總辦、幫總辦，俱各二人，章京八人，並以本處員司兼充。

translations.literal: Supervising directors, assistant supervising directors, chief managers, and assistant chief managers—two each; eight zhangjing—all concurrently filled by staff of this office.
translations.idiomatic: Two supervising directors, two assistant supervising directors, two chief managers, two assistant chief managers, and eight council clerks—all drawn from this office’s staff.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，附設財政處，尋罷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year a Fiscal Office was attached; soon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year a fiscal office was added, then soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 三十二年更名會議政務處，隸內閣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year renamed the Office for Conference on Government Affairs, subordinate to the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year it became the Conference on Government Affairs Office under the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年省。

translations.literal: Abolished in the third year of Xuantong.
translations.idiomatic: It was abolished in Xuantong 3.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，定署名制。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, a signing-by-name system was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year a system of signing by name was established.

sentences.zh: 越二年，設憲政編查館，覆命軍機大臣領之。

translations.literal: Two years later, the Constitutional Compilation and Inquiry Office was established, again ordering grand councillors to head it.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later a constitutional compilation and inquiry office was set up, again headed by grand councillors.

sentences.zh: 先是設考察政治館，命度支部尚書載澤等考察各國政治，至是更名。

translations.literal: Earlier the Political Investigation Office had been established, ordering Minister of the Metrics Section Zai Ze and others to investigate the politics of various states; at this time it was renamed.
translations.idiomatic: An office to study foreign politics had been set up earlier, with Metrics Minister Zai Ze and others sent abroad; it was now renamed.

sentences.zh: 置提調四；

translations.literal: Four supervising directors were established;
translations.idiomatic: Four supervising directors were appointed;

sentences.zh: 總核、參議各二；

translations.literal: two chief reviewers and two counsellors each;
translations.idiomatic: two chief reviewers and two counsellors;

sentences.zh: 庶務處總辦一；

translations.literal: one chief manager for the general affairs office;
translations.idiomatic: one chief manager oversaw general affairs;

sentences.zh: 一、二等諮議官，無恆額。

translations.literal: first- and second-grade advisory officials, without fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: first- and second-grade advisers, with no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 設編製、統計、官報三局，局長、副局長各一，科員視事酌置。

translations.literal: Three bureaus were established—for compilation, statistics, and official gazette—each with one director and one deputy director, with section members assigned as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Three bureaus were set up—for drafting, statistics, and the official gazette—each with a director and deputy, with section staff assigned as needed.

sentences.zh: 又考核科總辦一，幫辦正科員各二，副科員八，調京、外官兼充。

translations.literal: Also one chief manager for the examination section, two full assistant managers and two assistant chief section members each, eight deputy section members, with capital and provincial officials transferred to fill concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: An examination section had one chief manager, two full and two assistant section chiefs, and eight deputies, filled by officials transferred from the capital and provinces.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年省。

translations.literal: Abolished in the third year of Xuantong.
translations.idiomatic: It was abolished in Xuantong 3.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，改責任內閣，以軍機大臣為總協理大臣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong, the responsible cabinet was instituted, with grand councillors as chief coordinating ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 3 a responsible cabinet was introduced, with grand councillors as chief coordinating ministers.

sentences.zh: 內繙書房管理大臣，滿洲軍機大臣兼充，掌繙諭旨、御論、冊祝文字。

translations.literal: Ministers directing the Inner Translation Bureau—filled concurrently by Manchu grand councillors—managed translation of edicts, imperial discourses, and ritual texts for registers and prayers.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Translation Bureau was directed by Manchu grand councillors, who translated edicts, imperial essays, and ritual and prayer texts.

sentences.zh: 提調、協辦提調，各二人。

translations.literal: Supervising directors and assistant supervising directors—two each.
translations.idiomatic: Two supervising directors and two assistant supervising directors served.

sentences.zh: 收掌官、掌檔官，俱各四人。

translations.literal: Receiving officers and archive officers—four each.
translations.idiomatic: Four receiving officers and four archive officers served.

sentences.zh: 並於本房行走官內酌派。

translations.literal: All were assigned as appropriate from officials on duty in this bureau.
translations.idiomatic: They were chosen as needed from duty officers in the bureau.

sentences.zh: 繙譯四十人。

translations.literal: Forty translators.
translations.idiomatic: Forty translators served the bureau.

sentences.zh: 宣統初，改隸翰林院。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuantong, transferred to the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuantong it was placed under the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 方略館總裁，軍機大臣兼充。

translations.literal: Chief editor of the Military Campaign Records Office—filled concurrently by grand councillors.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign records office was headed by grand councillors serving concurrently as chief editors.

sentences.zh: 掌修方略。

translations.literal: Managed compilation of campaign records.
translations.idiomatic: It compiled official campaign narratives.

sentences.zh: 提調、收掌，俱滿、漢二人。

translations.literal: Supervising directors and receiving officers—two Manchus and two Han each.
translations.idiomatic: Two Manchu and two Han supervising directors and receiving officers served.

sentences.zh: 纂修，滿洲三人，漢六人。

translations.literal: Compilers—three Manchus and six Han.
translations.idiomatic: Three Manchu and six Han compilers served.

sentences.zh: 俱由軍機章京內派充。

translations.literal: All were assigned from among Grand Council zhangjing.
translations.idiomatic: All were detailed from Grand Council clerks.

sentences.zh: 漢纂修缺內由翰林院咨送充補一人。

translations.literal: Within Han compiler vacancies, one was filled by memorial transmission from the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: One Han compiler vacancy was filled on recommendation from the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 校對，無員限。

translations.literal: Proofreaders—no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Proofreaders had no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 六部司員、內閣中書兼充。

translations.literal: Filled concurrently by section members of the six ministries and Grand Secretariat secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry section members and secretariat secretaries served concurrently as proofreaders.

sentences.zh: 有事權置，畢乃省。

translations.literal: Established when needed with authority; cut when finished.
translations.idiomatic: Posts were created when needed and abolished when the work ended.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書，初制，滿洲一品，漢人二品。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel—in the initial system, Manchu first grade, Han second grade.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of Personnel was initially first grade for Manchus and second grade for Han officials.

sentences.zh: 順治十六年改滿尚書二品。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi Manchu ministers were changed to second grade.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 16 Manchu ministers were reduced to second grade.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年復故，九年仍改正二品。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi restored to former, in the ninth year still changed to regular second grade.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 6 the former ranks were restored; in Kangxi 9 Manchu ministers were again fixed at regular second grade.

sentences.zh: 雍正八年俱定從一品。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongzheng all fixed at subordinate first grade.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 8 all were fixed at subordinate first grade.

sentences.zh: 各部同。

translations.literal: The same for all ministries.
translations.idiomatic: All ministries followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 左、右侍郎，初制，滿洲、漢軍二品，漢員三品。

translations.literal: Left and right vice ministers—in the initial system, Manchu and Han Banner second grade, Han third grade.
translations.idiomatic: Left and right vice ministers were initially second grade for Manchus and Han Bannermen and third grade for Han officials.

sentences.zh: 順治十六年改滿侍郎三品。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi Manchu vice ministers were changed to third grade.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 16 Manchu vice ministers were reduced to third grade.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年復故，九年仍改正三品。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi restored to former, in the ninth year still changed to regular third grade.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 6 the former ranks were restored; in Kangxi 9 Manchu vice ministers were again fixed at regular third grade.

sentences.zh: 雍正八年俱定從二品。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongzheng all fixed at subordinate second grade.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 8 all were fixed at subordinate second grade.

sentences.zh: 各部同。

translations.literal: The same for all ministries.
translations.idiomatic: All ministries followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 俱滿、漢一人。

translations.literal: One Manchu and one Han each.
translations.idiomatic: Each ministry had one Manchu and one Han appointee.

sentences.zh: 其屬：堂主事，初制四品。

translations.literal: Subordinates: hall secretaries—in the initial system fourth grade.
translations.idiomatic: Among subordinates, hall secretaries were initially fourth grade.

sentences.zh: 順治十六年改六品。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi changed to sixth grade.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 16 they were reduced to sixth grade.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年升五品，九年定正六品。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi raised to fifth grade, in the ninth year fixed at regular sixth grade.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 6 they were raised to fifth grade; in Kangxi 9 fixed at regular sixth grade.

sentences.zh: 各部同。

translations.literal: The same for all ministries.
translations.idiomatic: All ministries followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 清檔房滿洲二人，漢本房滿洲二人，漢軍一人。

translations.literal: Manchu archive office two Manchus; Han memorial office two Manchus, one Han Bannerman.
translations.idiomatic: The Manchu archive office had two Manchus; the Han memorial office two Manchus and one Han Bannerman.

sentences.zh: 司務□司務，初制從九品。
