translations.idiomatic: Benyu was built in Kangxi 45.

sentences.zh: 曰儲濟，雍正六年建。

translations.literal: Chuji was built in the sixth year of Yongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chuji was built in Yongzheng 6.

sentences.zh: 曰豐益，七年建。

translations.literal: Fengyi was built in the seventh year.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyi was built in Yongzheng 7.

sentences.zh: 舊有萬安、裕豐，後省。

translations.literal: Wan'an and Yufeng formerly existed but were later cut.
translations.idiomatic: Wan'an and Yufeng had existed but were later abolished.

sentences.zh: 其恩豐倉，乾隆二十六年建，隸內府。

translations.literal: Enfeng Granary was built in the twenty-sixth year of Qianlong and was subordinate to the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeng Granary, built in Qianlong 26, was subordinate to the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 俱滿、漢各一人，各部院保送補用。

translations.literal: All had one Manchu and one Han each, filled by nomination from the ministries and courts.
translations.idiomatic: Each post had one Manchu and one Han, filled on nomination from ministries and courts.

sentences.zh: 掌分管京倉。

translations.literal: They managed their assigned capital granaries.
translations.idiomatic: They supervised assigned capital granaries.

sentences.zh: 中、西二倉監督，沿明制建。

translations.literal: Supervisors of the Central and Western granaries were established along the Ming system.
translations.idiomatic: Central and Western granary supervisors followed the Ming arrangement.

sentences.zh: 舊有南倉，後省。

translations.literal: The Southern Granary formerly existed but was later cut.
translations.idiomatic: A Southern Granary had existed but was later abolished.

sentences.zh: 滿、漢各一人，十一倉監督內調補。

translations.literal: One Manchu and one Han each, transferred from among the eleven granary supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: One Manchu and one Han each were transferred from the eleven capital granary supervisors.

sentences.zh: 掌分管通倉。

translations.literal: They managed their assigned Tongzhou granaries.
translations.idiomatic: They supervised assigned Tongzhou granaries.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，置漢侍郎一人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, one Han vice minister was established.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 one Han vice minister was appointed.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年省，十八年復。

translations.literal: Cut in the eighth year of Kangxi, restored in the eighteenth.
translations.idiomatic: The post was cut in Kangxi 8 and restored in Kangxi 18.

sentences.zh: 京、通各倉，戶部員司分理之。

translations.literal: Capital and Tongzhou granaries were divided among section officials of the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Capital and Tongzhou granaries were managed by Board of Revenue section officials.

sentences.zh: 通州坐糧□，十二年設京糧□。

translations.literal: At Tongzhou was the Grain Receipt Office (□); in the twelfth year the Beijing Grain Office (□) was established.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhou had the Grain Receipt Office (□); in the twelfth year the Beijing Grain Office (□) was set up.

sentences.zh: 十五年並入大通橋。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year both were merged into Datong Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year both were merged into Datong Bridge.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年置滿、漢監督各一人，尋省。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi one Manchu and one Han supervisor were appointed each, but soon cut.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 2 one Manchu and one Han supervisor were appointed each, then soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 四十七年復。

translations.literal: Restored in the forty-seventh year.
translations.idiomatic: They were restored in Kangxi 47.

sentences.zh: 以戶部官一人承其事。

translations.literal: One Board of Revenue official undertook the duties.
translations.idiomatic: One Board of Revenue official handled the work.

sentences.zh: 九年，置滿洲、漢軍侍郎各一人。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, one Manchu and one Han Banner vice minister were appointed each.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year one Manchu and one Han Banner vice minister were appointed each.

sentences.zh: 尋省漢軍缺。

translations.literal: The Han Banner post was soon cut.
translations.idiomatic: The Han Banner post was soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 十五年，定滿、漢各一人。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, fixed at one Manchu and one Han each.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the quota was fixed at one Manchu and one Han each.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十年，定京、通倉監督滿、漢各一人。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year of Kangxi, capital and Tongzhou granary supervisors were fixed at one Manchu and one Han each.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 50 capital and Tongzhou granary supervisors were fixed at one Manchu and one Han each.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年置副監督，尋省。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng deputy supervisors were established, but soon cut.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2 deputy supervisors were added, then soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 其缺由內閣中書、部院監寺官番選。

translations.literal: Their posts were filled in rotation from Grand Secretariat secretaries and ministry, court, and directorate officials.
translations.idiomatic: Vacancies were filled in rotation from secretariat secretaries and ministry, court, and directorate officials.

sentences.zh: 又初有總理，滿洲侍郎一人，與總漕並理漕務。

translations.literal: At first there was also a general superintendent—one Manchu vice minister—who jointly managed transport affairs with the Director-General of Grain Transport.
translations.idiomatic: There was also initially a general superintendent, one Manchu vice minister, who managed transport jointly with the Director-General of Grain Transport.

sentences.zh: 順治八年省，十二年復，十八年又省。

translations.literal: Cut in the eighth year of Shunzhi, restored in the twelfth, cut again in the eighteenth.
translations.idiomatic: It was cut in Shunzhi 8, restored in Shunzhi 12, and cut again in Shunzhi 18.

sentences.zh: 京師崇文門，正監督、副監督，左翼、右翼各一人。

translations.literal: At the capital, Chongwen Gate had a chief supervisor, deputy supervisor, and left and right wing supervisors, one each.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital Chongwen Gate had a chief supervisor, a deputy, and left- and right-wing supervisors, one each.

sentences.zh: 內府大臣及尚書侍郎兼充。

translations.literal: Filled concurrently by imperial household ministers and ministers or vice ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial household ministers and ministers or vice ministers served concurrently.

sentences.zh: 其各常關，或部臣題請特簡，或由京掣差部司官，或改令外官兼轄。

translations.literal: For the various routine customs stations, either a ministry official memorialized for special selection, or a capital ministry section official was drawn by lot, or outside officials were ordered to administer concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Routine customs stations were headed either by officials specially selected on ministry memorial, by capital section officials drawn by lot, or by outside officials ordered to administer them concurrently.

sentences.zh: 天津關，長蘆鹽政兼管。

translations.literal: Tianjin Pass was administered concurrently by the Changlu salt controller.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjin Pass was run concurrently by the Changlu salt controller.

sentences.zh: 通州，坐糧□兼管。

translations.literal: Tongzhou was administered concurrently by the Grain Receipt Office (□).
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhou was administered concurrently by the Grain Receipt Office (□).

sentences.zh: 張家口、殺虎口，部院司員兼充。

translations.literal: Zhangjiakou and Shahu Pass were filled concurrently by ministry and court section officials.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangjiakou and Shahu Pass were filled by ministry and court section officials serving concurrently.

sentences.zh: 潘桃口，多倫諾爾同知兼理。

translations.literal: Pantao Pass was administered by the subprefect of Dolon Nor.
translations.idiomatic: Pantao Pass was administered by the Dolon Nor subprefect.

sentences.zh: 龍泉、紫荊、喜峰、五虎、固關、白石、倒馬、茨溝、插箭嶺、馬水口，提督兼管，委參將、都司、守備、把總監收。

translations.literal: Longquan, Zijing, Xifeng, Wuhu, Guguan, Baishi, Daoma, Cigou, Chajianling, and Mashuikou were administered concurrently by the provincial military commander, with brigade generals, colonels, garrison commanders, and company commanders delegated to collect duties.
translations.idiomatic: Longquan, Zijing, Xifeng, Wuhu, Guguan, Baishi, Daoma, Cigou, Chajianling, and Mashuikou were overseen by the provincial commander, who delegated collection to brigade generals, colonels, garrison commanders, and company commanders.

sentences.zh: 三座塔、八溝、烏蘭哈達，理籓院司員兼充。

translations.literal: Sanzuota, Bagou, and Ulan Hada were filled concurrently by Court of Colonial Affairs section officials.
translations.idiomatic: Sanzuota, Bagou, and Ulan Hada were filled by Court of Colonial Affairs section officials serving concurrently.

sentences.zh: 奉天牛馬稅，部院司員兼充。

translations.literal: The Fengtian cattle-and-horse tax was filled concurrently by ministry and court section officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Fengtian cattle-and-horse tax was collected by ministry and court section officials serving concurrently.

sentences.zh: 中江，盛京將軍衙門章京及五部司員番選，後歸興鳳道兼理。

translations.literal: Zhongjiang was filled in rotation by zhangjing of the Shengjing general's yamen and section officials of the five boards; later it was administered by the Xingfeng circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjiang was filled in rotation by clerks of the Shengjing general's yamen and section officials of the five boards; later it passed to the Xingfeng circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 臨清，巡撫兼管，委知州監收。

translations.literal: Linqing was administered concurrently by the governor, with the prefect delegated to collect duties.
translations.idiomatic: Linqing was run by the governor, with collection delegated to the prefect.

sentences.zh: 歸化城，巡撫兼管，委道員監收。

translations.literal: Guihuacheng was administered concurrently by the governor, with a circuit intendant delegated to collect duties.
translations.idiomatic: Guihuacheng was run by the governor, with collection delegated to a circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 潼關，道員兼理。

translations.literal: Tong Pass was administered by a circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Pass was administered by a circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 滸墅關，蘇州織造監理。

translations.literal: Hushu Pass was supervised by the Suzhou weaving commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Hushu Pass was supervised by the Suzhou weaving commissioner.

sentences.zh: 淮安關兼廟灣口，內府司員兼充。

translations.literal: Huai'an Pass, including Miaowan Pass, was filled concurrently by an imperial household section official.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'an Pass, including Miaowan, was filled by an imperial household section official serving concurrently.

sentences.zh: 揚關，巡撫兼管，委淮揚海道兼收。

translations.literal: Yangzhou Pass was administered concurrently by the governor, with the Huai-Yang maritime circuit intendant collecting duties.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou Pass was run by the governor, with collection by the Huai-Yang maritime circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 西新關，江寧織造兼理，後改歸巡撫。

translations.literal: Xixin Pass was administered by the Jiangning weaving commissioner and later transferred to the governor.
translations.idiomatic: Xixin Pass was run by the Jiangning weaving commissioner and later transferred to the governor.

sentences.zh: 鳳陽關，皖北道兼理。

translations.literal: Fengyang Pass was administered by the Northern Anhui circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyang Pass was administered by the Northern Anhui circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 贛關，巡撫兼管，委吉南贛寧道監收。

translations.literal: Gan Pass was administered concurrently by the governor, with the Ji-Nan-Gan-Ning circuit intendant delegated to collect duties.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Pass was run by the governor, with collection delegated to the Ji-Nan-Gan-Ning circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 閩安關，巡撫兼管，後改歸總督，委福州府同知監收。

translations.literal: Min'an Pass was administered concurrently by the governor, later transferred to the governor-general, with the Tongzhi of Fuzhou Prefecture delegated to collect duties.
translations.idiomatic: Min'an Pass was run by the governor, later by the governor-general, with collection delegated to the Fuzhou prefectural vice prefect.

sentences.zh: 北新關，杭州織造兼管，後改歸巡撫。

translations.literal: Beixin Pass was administered concurrently by the Hangzhou weaving commissioner and later transferred to the governor.
translations.idiomatic: Beixin Pass was run by the Hangzhou weaving commissioner and later transferred to the governor.

sentences.zh: 武昌廠、荊關，巡撫兼管，後改歸總督委員監收。

translations.literal: Wuchang Depot and Jing Pass were administered concurrently by the governor and later transferred to commissioners appointed by the governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang Depot and Jing Pass were run by the governor and later by commissioners appointed by the governor-general.

sentences.zh: 夔關，總督兼管，委知府監收。

translations.literal: Kui Pass was administered concurrently by the governor-general, with the prefect delegated to collect duties.
translations.idiomatic: Kui Pass was run by the governor-general, with collection delegated to the prefect.

sentences.zh: 打箭爐，同知兼理。

translations.literal: Dartsendo was administered by a subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: Dartsendo was administered by a subprefect.

sentences.zh: 太平關，巡撫兼管，委南韶連道監收。

translations.literal: Taiping Pass was administered concurrently by the governor, with the Nan-Shao-Lian circuit intendant delegated to collect duties.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping Pass was run by the governor, with collection delegated to the Nan-Shao-Lian circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 梧廠、潯廠，巡撫兼管，委梧、潯二知府監收。

translations.literal: Wuzhou and Xun depots were administered concurrently by the governor, with the prefects of Wuzhou and Xunzhou delegated to collect duties.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou and Xun depots were run by the governor, with collection delegated to the prefects of Wuzhou and Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 初制，榷百貨者曰戶關，榷竹木船鈔者曰工關，為戶、工二部分司，後改今制。

translations.literal: In the initial system, customs levying general merchandise were called revenue customs, and those levying timber, boats, and boat licenses were called works customs; they were divided between the Revenue and Works ministries, later changed to the present system.
translations.idiomatic: Originally commodity customs were called revenue customs and timber-and-shipping customs works customs, split between the Revenue and Works ministries until the present system replaced them.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，工關多改稱常關，唯直隸等省名稱如故。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong, many works customs were renamed routine customs, except in Zhili and certain provinces where the old names remained.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 3 many works customs were renamed routine customs, though Zhili and some provinces kept the old names.

sentences.zh: 並隸度支部。

translations.literal: All were placed under the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: All were placed under the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 往例以內府官簡充。

translations.literal: Formerly imperial household officials were specially selected.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly imperial household officials were specially chosen.

sentences.zh: 乾隆間，改令內務府大臣為之。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong period, ministers of the Imperial Household Department were ordered to fill the posts instead.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianlong, ministers of the Imperial Household Department were ordered to fill them instead.

sentences.zh: 後部院大臣並得簡充，定為滿洲員缺。

translations.literal: Later ministry and court grand ministers could also be specially selected; the posts were fixed as Manchu-quota positions.
translations.idiomatic: Later ministry and court grand ministers could also be chosen; the posts were fixed as Manchu-quota positions.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書，左、右侍郎，俱滿、漢一人。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites and left and right vice ministers—one Manchu and one Han each.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of Rites and left and right vice ministers each had one Manchu and one Han appointee.

sentences.zh: 其屬：堂主事，清檔房滿洲二人，漢本房滿洲、漢軍各一人。

translations.literal: Subordinates: hall secretaries—the Manchu archive office two Manchus; the Han memorial office one Manchu and one Han Bannerman each.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates included hall secretaries: two Manchus in the Manchu archive office; in the Han memorial office one Manchu and one Han Bannerman each.

sentences.zh: 司務□司務，滿、漢各一人。

translations.literal: Registry managers (□), one Manchu and one Han each.
translations.idiomatic: Registry managers (□), one Manchu and one Han each.

sentences.zh: 筆帖式，宗室一人，滿洲三十有四人，蒙古二人，漢軍四人。

translations.literal: Clerks: one imperial clansman, thirty-four Manchus, two Mongols, and four Han Bannermen.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks numbered one imperial clansman, thirty-four Manchus, two Mongols, and four Han Bannermen.

sentences.zh: 典制、祠祭、主客、精膳四清吏司：郎中，滿洲六人，典制、祠祭，各二人，餘俱一人。

translations.literal: The four Qing secretariats—Rites and Regulations, Sacrifices, Foreign Guests, and Fine Foods: directors—six Manchus; Rites and Regulations and Sacrifices two each, the rest one each.
translations.idiomatic: The four Qing secretariats—Rites and Regulations, Sacrifices, Foreign Guests, and Fine Foods—had six Manchu directors: two each for Rites and Regulations and Sacrifices, one each for the others.

sentences.zh: 蒙古一人，主客司置。

translations.literal: One Mongol, established in the Foreign Guests Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: One Mongol post was established in the Foreign Guests Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 漢四人。

translations.literal: Four Han.
translations.idiomatic: Four Han officials served.

sentences.zh: 司各一人。

translations.literal: One in each secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: One served in each secretariat.

sentences.zh: 員外郎，宗室一人，主客司置。

translations.literal: Vice directors: one imperial clansman, established in the Foreign Guests Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Vice directors included one imperial clansman in the Foreign Guests Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 滿洲八人，典制、祠祭司各三人。

translations.literal: Eight Manchus—three each in the Rites and Regulations and Sacrifices secretariats.
translations.idiomatic: Eight Manchus served—three each in Rites and Regulations and Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 餘俱一人。

translations.literal: One each for the rest.
translations.idiomatic: The rest had one each.

sentences.zh: 蒙古一人，祠祭司置。

translations.literal: One Mongol, established in the Sacrifices Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: One Mongol post was established in the Sacrifices Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 漢二人。

translations.literal: Two Han.
translations.idiomatic: Two Han officials served.

sentences.zh: 典制、祠祭司各一人。

translations.literal: One each in the Ceremonial Regulations and Sacrificial Rites bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: The Ceremonial Regulations and Sacrificial Rites bureaus each had one.

sentences.zh: 主事，宗室、蒙古各一人，精膳司置。

translations.literal: Section chiefs: one each from the imperial clan and Mongols, established in the Refined Provisions Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Section chiefs included one imperial-clansman and one Mongol, both in the Refined Provisions Bureau.

sentences.zh: 滿洲三人，典制、祠祭、精膳司各一人。

translations.literal: Three Manchus, one each in the Ceremonial Regulations, Sacrificial Rites, and Refined Provisions bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Three Manchu section chiefs, one in each of the Ceremonial Regulations, Sacrificial Rites, and Refined Provisions bureaus.

sentences.zh: 漢四人。

translations.literal: Four Han Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Four Han appointees.

sentences.zh: 司各一人。

translations.literal: One in each bureau.
translations.idiomatic: One per bureau.

sentences.zh: 印鑄局，漢員外郎、滿洲署主事、漢大使，未入流。

translations.literal: Seal Casting Office: one Han vice director, one Manchu acting section chief, and one Han envoy, all below the regular grades.
translations.idiomatic: The Seal Casting Office had a Han vice director, a Manchu acting section chief, and a Han envoy, none in the regular grade series.

sentences.zh: 各一人。

translations.literal: One each.
translations.idiomatic: One of each.

sentences.zh: 堂子尉，滿洲八人。

translations.literal: Tangzi guards, eight Manchus.
translations.idiomatic: Eight Manchu tangzi guards.

sentences.zh: 七品二人，八品六人。

translations.literal: Two of seventh rank and six of eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two at seventh rank and six at eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 尚書掌五禮秩敘，典領學校貢舉，以布邦教。

translations.literal: The minister directed the ordering of the five rites, oversaw schools and the civil examinations, and spread state instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The minister ordered the five rites, supervised schools and examinations, and spread the dynasty’s teaching.

sentences.zh: 侍郎貳之。

translations.literal: The vice ministers assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice ministers served as his deputies.

sentences.zh: 典制掌嘉禮、軍禮。

translations.literal: Ceremonial Regulations handled auspicious rites and military rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Ceremonial Regulations Bureau managed auspicious and military rites.

sentences.zh: 稽彝章，辨名數，頒式諸司。

translations.literal: It checked ritual statutes, distinguished titles and numbers, and issued models to all bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: It audited ritual codes, fixed names and ranks, and promulgated forms to the ministries.

sentences.zh: 三歲大比，司其名籍。

translations.literal: At the triennial great comparison it kept the name registers.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years at the metropolitan examination it maintained the registers of candidates.

sentences.zh: 四方忠孝貞義，訪懋旌閭。

translations.literal: For loyalty, filial piety, chastity, and righteousness throughout the realm, it sought out merit and ordered commendation in the lanes.
translations.idiomatic: It sought out the loyal, filial, chaste, and righteous across the empire and arranged neighborhood commendations.

sentences.zh: 祠祭掌吉禮、凶禮。

translations.literal: Sacrificial Rites handled felicitous rites and mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Sacrificial Rites Bureau managed felicitous and mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 凡大祀、中祀、群祀，以歲時辨其序事與其用等。

translations.literal: For all great, middle, and group sacrifices, it distinguished by season the sequence of services and their grades of expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: For great, middle, and collective sacrifices it set seasonal order of rites and scales of provision.

sentences.zh: 日月交食，內外諸司救護；

translations.literal: When sun and moon eclipsed, inner and outer offices performed rescue rites;
translations.idiomatic: On solar and lunar eclipses all offices within and without the capital performed protective rites;

sentences.zh: 有災異即奏聞。

translations.literal: when omens or disasters occurred it reported at once.
translations.idiomatic: any portent or disaster was reported immediately.

sentences.zh: 凡喪葬、祭祀，貴賤有等，皆定程式而頒行之。

translations.literal: For all funerals and sacrifices, noble and humble had their grades; it fixed procedures and promulgated them.
translations.idiomatic: Funerals and sacrifices were graded by status; it codified procedures and issued them.

sentences.zh: 勳戚、文武大臣請葬祭、贈謚，必移所司覈行。

translations.literal: When meritorious kinsmen and civil or military grandees requested burial rites, sacrifices, or posthumous titles, the matter had to be transferred to the responsible bureau for verification and execution.
translations.idiomatic: Burial, sacrifice, or posthumous honors for meritorious kin and high ministers required referral to the proper bureau for review.

sentences.zh: 並籍領史祝、醫巫、音樂、僧道，司其禁令，有妖妄者罪無赦。

translations.literal: It also registered and oversaw historiographers, invokers, physicians and shamans, musicians, and Buddhist and Daoist clergy, enforced their prohibitions, and showed no mercy to those guilty of sorcery or false doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: It also licensed historians, prayer-officers, healers, musicians, and clergy, enforced their rules, and punished sorcery without pardon.

sentences.zh: 主客掌賓禮。

translations.literal: Guest Reception handled guest rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Guest Reception Bureau managed rites for foreign guests.

sentences.zh: 凡蕃使朝貢，館餼賜予，辨其貢道遠邇、貢使多寡、貢物豐約以定。

translations.literal: For all tributary envoys from the borderlands, lodging, provisions, and gifts were set by distinguishing the distance of the tribute route, the number of envoys, and the abundance of tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: Tributary missions received lodging, food, and gifts scaled to route distance, embassy size, and tribute volume.

sentences.zh: 頒實錄、玉牒告成褒賞。

translations.literal: It issued rewards when the Veritable Records or Imperial Genealogy were completed.
translations.idiomatic: It distributed commendations on completion of the Veritable Records or Imperial Genealogy.

sentences.zh: 稽霍茶歲額。

translations.literal: It audited the annual quota of Huo tea.
translations.idiomatic: It checked annual tea allotments.

sentences.zh: 精膳掌五禮燕饗與其牲牷。

translations.literal: Refined Provisions handled banquets of the five rites and their sacrificial victims.
translations.idiomatic: The Refined Provisions Bureau managed five-rites banquets and sacrificial livestock.

sentences.zh: 賜百官禮食，視品秩以為差，光祿供膳羞，會計其數而程其出納，匯覈各司。

translations.literal: Ceremonial food granted to officials differed by rank; the Court of Imperial Entertainments supplied dishes, the numbers were reckoned and disbursement scheduled, and accounts were consolidated for all bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Officials received graded ritual meals; the Court of Imperial Entertainments furnished them, tallied quantities, scheduled issue, and reported to all bureaus.

sentences.zh: 鑄印局題銷鑄印，掌鑄寶璽，凡內外諸司印信，並范冶之。

translations.literal: The Seal Casting Office handled memorials to cancel and recast seals, cast imperial seals and treasure, and for all inner and outer offices it cast their seals.
translations.idiomatic: The Seal Casting Office processed seal cancellations and recasting, cast imperial seals, and forged seals for all agencies.

sentences.zh: 用銀質直鈕三台者：宗人府、衍聖公，清、漢文尚方大篆，方三寸三分，厚一寸；

translations.literal: Those using silver with a straight knob and three platforms: the Court of the Imperial Clan and the Duke of Confucius, in Qing and Han Shangfang great seal script, square three cun three fen, one cun thick;
translations.idiomatic: Silver seals with straight knobs and triple platforms went to the Imperial Clan Court and the Duke of Confucius: Qing and Han Shangfang great seal script, 3.3 cun square, 1 cun thick;

sentences.zh: 六部、戶部鹽茶、都察院、行在部院，清、漢、蒙三體字，清、漢文尚方大篆，蒙文不篆，方三寸三分，厚九分。

translations.literal: the Six Ministries, the Ministry of Revenue’s Salt and Tea office, the Censorate, and acting ministries in the provinces, in Qing, Han, and Mongol scripts, Qing and Han in Shangfang great seal script with Mongol unsealed, square three cun three fen, nine fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: the Six Ministries, Revenue Salt and Tea, the Censorate, and provincial acting ministries used trilingual seals in Shangfang great script (Mongol unsealed), 3.3 cun square, 0.9 cun thick.

sentences.zh: 直鈕二台者：盛京五部、戶部三庫，清、漢文尚方大篆，方三寸三分，厚八分；

translations.literal: Straight knob, two platforms: the five Mukden ministries and the three Revenue treasuries, Qing and Han Shangfang great seal script, square three cun three fen, eight fen thick;
translations.idiomatic: Two-platform straight knobs: Mukden’s five ministries and Revenue’s three treasuries, Qing and Han Shangfang great script, 3.3 cun square, 0.8 cun thick;

sentences.zh: 軍機處、內務府、盛京內務府、翰林院、鑾輿衛，清、漢文尚方大篆，方三寸二分，厚八分。

translations.literal: Grand Council, Imperial Household, Mukden Imperial Household, Hanlin Academy, and Imperial Carriage Guard, Qing and Han Shangfang great seal script, square three cun two fen, eight fen thick.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Council, Imperial Household, Mukden Household, Hanlin Academy, and Carriage Guard used Qing-Han Shangfang great script seals, 3.2 cun square, 0.8 cun thick.

sentences.zh: 虎鈕三台者：提督、總兵。

translations.literal: Tiger knob, three platforms: provincial military governors and regional commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Triple-platform tiger-knob seals went to governors-general and commanders-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 虎鈕二台者：侯、伯、領侍衛內大臣、都統、前鋒統領、護軍統領、步軍統領、總管火器營神機營、圓明園總營八旗包衣三旗官兵、經略大臣、大將軍、鎮守將軍、科布多參贊大臣、鎮守掛印總兵，清、漢文柳葉篆；

translations.literal: In the ninth year four were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Four were cut in year 9.

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kangxi transferred to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 10 they were moved to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 皇史宬尉，正七品。

translations.literal: Archives guards of the Imperial Historical Archives, regular seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Archives guards ranked at regular seventh grade.

sentences.zh: 滿洲三人。

translations.literal: Three Manchus.
translations.idiomatic: Three Manchus served.

translations.literal: Sacrificial livestock officers, regular seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial-livestock officers held regular seventh rank.

sentences.zh: 蒙古二人。

sentences.zh: 光緒二十四年，省光祿、鴻臚二寺入之，尋復故。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Guangxu the Courts of Imperial Entertainments and State Ceremonial were cut and merged into it, but soon restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 24 the Courts of Imperial Entertainments and State Ceremonial were absorbed into the ministry, then soon restored.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，詔罷科舉，各省學政改隸學務大臣，自是釐正士風之責，不屬本部矣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year an edict abolished the civil examinations; provincial education commissioners were placed under the Commissioner of Education, and from then on responsibility for rectifying scholar-official conduct no longer belonged to this ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year examinations were abolished by edict, provincial education commissioners were placed under the Commissioner of Education, and responsibility for rectifying scholar-official conduct no longer rested with this ministry.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，以光祿、太常、鴻臚三寺同為執禮官，仍省入。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year the three courts—Imperial Entertainments, Imperial Sacrifices, and State Ceremonial—were alike made ritual officers and again merged in.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year the courts of Imperial Entertainments, Imperial Sacrifices, and State Ceremonial were all treated as ritual officers and again absorbed into the ministry.

sentences.zh: 更精膳司曰光祿，主客司曰太常，並各置郎中、員外郎、主事各一人。

translations.literal: The Fine Foods Secretariat was renamed Guanglu, the Foreign Guests Secretariat Taichang, and each was given one director, vice director, and secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The Fine Foods Secretariat was renamed Guanglu and the Foreign Guests Secretariat Taichang, each receiving one director, vice director, and secretary.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚事稍簡，歸入典制司，增員外郎一人，並滿、漢參用。

translations.literal: State Ceremonial affairs were somewhat lighter and were returned to the Rites and Regulations Secretariat; one vice director was added, with Manchu and Han used jointly.
translations.idiomatic: State Ceremonial duties, being lighter, were folded into the Rites and Regulations Secretariat, which gained one vice director filled jointly by Manchu and Han officials.

sentences.zh: 是歲定尚書，侍郎，左、右丞、參員額如吏部。

translations.literal: That year quotas for the minister, vice ministers, and left and right assistants and commissioners were fixed like those of the Board of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: That year the quotas for minister, vice ministers, and left and right assistants and commissioners were fixed to match the Board of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 設禮器庫，置郎中、員外郎各一人，贊禮官、讀祝官亦如之。

translations.literal: A Rites Implements Repository was established with one director and one vice director; eulogy officers and prayer readers were likewise appointed.
translations.idiomatic: A Rites Implements Repository was set up with one director and one vice director, and eulogy and prayer-reading officers were appointed on the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 俱六品。

translations.literal: All were sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: All held sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 太常寺丞改充。

translations.literal: Filled by vice directors of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: They were filled by vice directors of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 簿正、光祿寺署正改充。

translations.literal: Filled by recorders and acting directors of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: They were filled by recorders and acting directors of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 典簿太常寺博士改充者三人，光祿寺典簿改充者一人。

translations.literal: Of recordkeepers, three were filled by doctors of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and one by a recordkeeper of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Three recordkeepers were drawn from doctors of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and one from a recordkeeper of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 各四人，司庫二人，太常、光祿兩寺司庫改充。

translations.literal: Four each; two warehouse keepers, filled by warehouse keepers of the Taichang and Guanglu courts.
translations.idiomatic: There were four in each category and two warehouse keepers, drawn from the Taichang and Guanglu courts.

sentences.zh: 以上品秩俱如舊。

translations.literal: The ranks of all the above remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: All of the above retained their former ranks.

sentences.zh: 筆帖式十有四人。

translations.literal: Fourteen clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen clerks served.

sentences.zh: 三寺內揀選酌留。

translations.literal: Selected and retained as appropriate from within the three courts.
translations.idiomatic: They were chosen and retained as appropriate from staff of the three courts.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，避帝諱，改儀制司曰典制。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong, to avoid the imperial taboo name, the Ceremonial Regulations Secretariat was renamed Rites and Regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 1, to avoid the imperial taboo, the Ceremonial Regulations Secretariat was renamed Rites and Regulations.

sentences.zh: 初制，禮部設馬館，置正、副監督各一人。

translations.literal: In the initial system the Ministry of Rites established a Horse Office with one chief supervisor and one deputy supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Under the initial system the Ministry of Rites set up a Horse Office with one chief and one deputy supervisor.

sentences.zh: 正監督，本部司員充。

translations.literal: The chief supervisor was filled by a section official of this ministry.
translations.idiomatic: The chief supervisor was a section official of this ministry.

sentences.zh: 副監督，理籓院司員充。

translations.literal: The deputy supervisor was filled by a section official of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy supervisor was a section official of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十七年，省入理籓院。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Qianlong it was cut and merged into the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 27 it was abolished and absorbed into the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 又初置滿洲宣表官四人，後減二人，尋並入太常寺。

translations.literal: At first four Manchu proclamation officers were established; later two were cut, and soon the post was merged into the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Four Manchu proclamation officers were first appointed, later reduced by two, and soon the office was merged into the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 會同四譯館，滿洲稽察大臣二人，部院司寺堂官內簡派。

translations.literal: For the Combined Reception and Four Translation Offices, two Manchu inspecting grand ministers were specially selected from bureau chiefs of ministries, courts, and directorates.
translations.idiomatic: The Combined Reception and Four Translation Offices had two Manchu inspecting grand ministers chosen from bureau chiefs of ministries, courts, and directorates.

sentences.zh: 提督館事兼鴻臚寺少卿一人，禮部郎中內選補。

translations.literal: One superintendent of the offices who also served as vice director of the Court of State Ceremonial was selected from directors of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: One superintendent of the offices, concurrently vice director of the Court of State Ceremonial, was chosen from directors of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 掌治賓客，諭言語。

translations.literal: He managed guests and instructed them in language.
translations.idiomatic: He received foreign guests and instructed them in protocol and language.

sentences.zh: 漢大使一人，正九品。

translations.literal: One Han envoy, regular ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: One Han envoy of regular ninth rank served.

sentences.zh: 正教、序班漢二人，朝鮮通事官八人。

translations.literal: Two Han chief instructors and protocol ushers, and eight Korean interpreters.
translations.idiomatic: There were two Han chief instructors and protocol ushers and eight Korean interpreters.

sentences.zh: 六品、七品各二人，八品四人。

translations.literal: Two of sixth rank and two of seventh rank each, and four of eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Two held sixth rank, two seventh rank, and four eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，會同四譯分設二館。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi the Combined Office and Four Translation Offices were split into two bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 the combined reception and translation offices were split into two bureaus.

sentences.zh: 會同館隸禮部，以主客司主事滿、漢各一人提督之。

translations.literal: The Reception Office was subordinate to the Ministry of Rites, supervised by one Manchu and one Han secretary of the Foreign Guests Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The Reception Office reported to the Ministry of Rites and was supervised by one Manchu and one Han secretary of the Foreign Guests Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 四譯館隸翰林院，以太常寺漢少卿一人提督之。

translations.literal: The Four Translation Offices were subordinate to the Hanlin Academy, supervised by one Han vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The Four Translation Offices reported to the Hanlin Academy under one Han vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 分設回回、緬甸、百夷、西番、高昌、西天、八百、暹羅八館，以譯遠方朝貢文字。

translations.literal: Eight offices were set up—Hui, Burma, Baiyi, Xifan, Gaochang, Xitian, Babai, and Siam—to translate tribute documents from distant regions.
translations.idiomatic: Eight offices—Hui, Burma, Baiyi, Xifan, Gaochang, Xitian, Babai, and Siam—translated tribute documents from distant lands.

sentences.zh: 置序班二十人，十五年定正教、協教各八人。

translations.literal: Twenty protocol ushers were appointed; in the fifteenth year chief and assistant instructors were fixed at eight each.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty protocol ushers were appointed; in the fifteenth year chief and assistant instructors were fixed at eight each.

sentences.zh: 康熙間省至九人，以一人管典務□事。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi period the number was cut to nine, with one person managing canonical duties (□).
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi the staff was reduced to nine, one of whom managed canonical duties (□).

sentences.zh: 乾隆十三年，省典務一人，序班六人，額定二人。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong one canonical-duty officer and six protocol ushers were cut, and the quota was fixed at two.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 13 one canonical-duty officer and six protocol ushers were cut, fixing the quota at two.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮通事官六人。

translations.literal: Six Korean interpreters.
translations.idiomatic: Six Korean interpreters served.

sentences.zh: 後增十人。

translations.literal: Later ten were added.
translations.idiomatic: Ten more were added later.

sentences.zh: 凡六品十人、七品六人。

translations.literal: In all, ten of sixth rank and six of seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: In all there were ten sixth-rank and six seventh-rank posts.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十三年省六品四人、七品二人，增八品二人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Qianlong four sixth-rank and two seventh-rank posts were cut, and two eighth-rank posts were added.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 23 four sixth-rank and two seventh-rank posts were cut and two eighth-rank posts added.

sentences.zh: 後俱省。

translations.literal: Later all were cut.
translations.idiomatic: Later all were abolished.

sentences.zh: 十四年，置員外郎品級通事一人，掌會同館印。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year one interpreter of vice-director rank was established to keep the seal of the Reception Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year one interpreter of vice-director rank was appointed to keep the Reception Office seal.

sentences.zh: 尋省。

translations.literal: Soon cut.
translations.idiomatic: The post was soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十三年，省四譯館入禮部，更名會同四譯館，改八館為二，曰西域，曰百夷，以禮部郎中兼鴻臚寺少卿銜一人攝之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong the Four Translation Offices were cut and merged into the Ministry of Rites, renamed the Combined Reception and Four Translation Offices; the eight offices were changed to two, called Western Regions and Baiyi, with one director of the Ministry of Rites who also held the vice-directorship of the Court of State Ceremonial acting in charge.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 13 the Four Translation Offices were absorbed into the Ministry of Rites as the Combined Reception and Four Translation Offices; the eight offices became two—the Western Regions and Baiyi—with one ministry director concurrently holding the Court of State Ceremonial vice-directorship in charge.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十九年省。

translations.literal: Cut in the twenty-ninth year of Guangxu.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished in Guangxu 29.

sentences.zh: 樂部，典樂大臣無員限，禮部滿洲尚書一人兼之。

translations.literal: The Music Directorate had no fixed quota for directors of music; one Manchu minister of the Ministry of Rites held the post concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: The Music Directorate had no fixed quota of music directors; one Manchu minister of Rites served concurrently.

sentences.zh: 後改各部侍郎、內務府大臣兼理。

translations.literal: Later vice ministers of various ministries and ministers of the Imperial Household Department administered it concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Later vice ministers of various ministries and imperial household ministers took charge concurrently.

sentences.zh: 又滿洲王大臣知樂者，亦曰管理大臣。

translations.literal: Manchu princes and grand ministers who understood music were also called managing grand ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Manchu princes and grand ministers versed in music were also styled managing grand ministers.

sentences.zh: 掌考樂律樂均度數，協之以聲歌，播之以器物。

translations.literal: They examined pitch, temperament, and measure, harmonized them with song, and spread them through instruments.
translations.idiomatic: They examined pitch, temperament, and measure, coordinated them with vocal music, and deployed them through instruments.

sentences.zh: 辨祭祀、朝會、燕饗之用，以格幽明，和上下。

translations.literal: They distinguished uses for sacrifices, court audiences, and banquets, thereby reaching the hidden and manifest and harmonizing high and low.
translations.idiomatic: They assigned music for sacrifices, court audiences, and banquets, thereby linking the seen and unseen and harmonizing high and low.

sentences.zh: 神樂署，署正一人，正六品。

translations.literal: The Divine Music Office had one director, regular sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Divine Music Office had one director of regular sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 左、右署丞各一人，從八品。

translations.literal: Left and right deputy directors, one each, secondary eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Left and right deputy directors, one each, held secondary eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 協律郎五人，正八品。

translations.literal: Five pitch regulators, regular eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Five pitch regulators of regular eighth rank served.

sentences.zh: 司樂二十有五人。

translations.literal: Twenty-five music officers.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-five music officers served.

sentences.zh: 正九品。

translations.literal: Regular ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: They held regular ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 凡樂生百八十人、舞生三百人屬之，俱漢員，兼隸太常寺，掌郊廟、祠祭諸樂。

translations.literal: One hundred eighty musicians and three hundred dancers were subordinate to it—all Han posts—also subordinate to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, managing suburban, temple, and sacrificial music.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred eighty musicians and three hundred dancers reported to it—all Han appointees—also under the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, managing suburban, temple, and sacrificial music.

sentences.zh: 和聲署，署正、署丞，俱滿、漢各一人。

translations.literal: The Harmonious Sounds Office had one director and one deputy director each, one Manchu and one Han.
translations.idiomatic: The Harmonious Sounds Office had one Manchu and one Han director and deputy director each.

sentences.zh: 滿員，內務府郎中、員外郎兼充。

translations.literal: Manchu posts were filled concurrently by directors and vice directors of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: Manchu posts were filled concurrently by directors and vice directors of the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 漢員，禮部郎中、員外郎兼充。

translations.literal: Han posts were filled concurrently by directors and vice directors of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Han posts were filled concurrently by directors and vice directors of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 凡供用官三十人，本署八人。

translations.literal: Thirty service officials in all, eight belonging to the office itself.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty service officials served in all, eight belonging to the office itself.

sentences.zh: 禮部筆帖式兼充二人，內務府贊禮郎兼充六人，筆帖式及各項有品級者兼充十有二人，鴻臚寺鳴贊官兼充二人。

translations.literal: Two were filled concurrently by clerks of the Ministry of Rites; six by eulogy officers of the Imperial Household Department; twelve by clerks and various ranked officials; and two by announcing officers of the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: Two were ministry clerks on concurrent duty; six imperial household eulogy officers; twelve clerks and other ranked officials; and two announcing officers of the Court of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 署史長十有六人，署史百四十有八人屬之，掌殿廷朝會、燕饗諸樂。

translations.literal: Sixteen chief office scribes and one hundred forty-eight office scribes were subordinate to it, managing palace-court, audience, and banquet music.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen chief scribes and one hundred forty-eight scribes reported to it, managing music for palace audiences and banquets.

sentences.zh: 其宮廷之樂，內務府掌禮司中和樂處典之。

translations.literal: Palace music was managed by the Central Harmony Music Office of the Rites Section of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: Palace music was managed by the Central Harmony Music Office of the imperial household Rites Section.

sentences.zh: 鹵簿之樂，鑾輿衛、旗手衛校尉典之。

translations.literal: Music for the imperial guard of honor was managed by guards of the Imperial Carriage Guard and Banner Hand Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Music for the imperial procession was managed by guards of the Imperial Carriage Guard and Banner Hand Guard.

sentences.zh: 並隸以部。

translations.literal: All were likewise subordinate to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: All were likewise under the ministry's oversight.

sentences.zh: 什傍處，掇爾契達一人，兼三等侍衛。

translations.literal: The Shibang Office had one duo'erqida, who also served as a third-rank bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: The Shibang Office had one duo'erqida who also held third-rank bodyguard rank.

sentences.zh: 六品銜達、七品銜達各二人。

translations.literal: Two rank-bearing officers of sixth-rank brevet and two of seventh-rank brevet.
translations.idiomatic: Two brevet sixth-rank and two brevet seventh-rank officers served.

sentences.zh: 拜唐阿六十人，兼隸侍衛處。

translations.literal: Sixty bayantai, also subordinate to the Bodyguard Office.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty bayantai also reported to the Bodyguard Office.

sentences.zh: 掌奏掇爾多密之樂，燕饗列之。

translations.literal: They performed duo'erduomi music and were arrayed at banquets.
translations.idiomatic: They performed duo'erduomi music and were arrayed at banquets.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，置教坊司，奉鑾一人，左、右韶舞，左、右司樂各一人，協同十人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi the Music Training Office was established, with one chief musician, left and right dance masters, left and right music officers, and ten assistants.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 the Music Training Office was set up with one chief musician, left and right dance masters, left and right music officers, and ten assistants.

sentences.zh: 以上並正九品。

translations.literal: All the above were regular ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: All of the above held regular ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 俳長無定員。

translations.literal: Lead players had no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Lead players had no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 未入流。

translations.literal: Outside the regular ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Their posts lay outside the regular bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 太常寺神樂觀，漢提點一人，正六品。

translations.literal: The Divine Music Observatory of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices had one Han intendant, regular sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices' Divine Music Observatory had one Han intendant of regular sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 左、右知觀各一人，正八品。

translations.literal: Left and right observatory directors, one each, regular eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Left and right observatory directors, one each, held regular eighth rank.

sentences.zh: 漢協律郎五人。

translations.literal: Five Han pitch regulators.
translations.idiomatic: Five Han pitch regulators served.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十八年省。

translations.literal: Cut in the thirty-eighth year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished in Kangxi 38.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年復故。

translations.literal: Restored in the first year of Yongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Restored in Yongzheng 1.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年增三人，九年省六人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianlong three were added; in the ninth year six were cut.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 2 three were added; in Qianlong 9 six were cut.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年增二人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing two were added.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4 two were added.

sentences.zh: 道光元年增二人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang two were added.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 1 two were added.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年增二人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng two were added.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 2 two were added.

sentences.zh: 雍正七年，改教坊司為和樂署，省奉鑾各官。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongzheng the Music Training Office was renamed the Harmonious Music Office, and the chief musician and related posts were cut.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 7 the Music Training Office became the Harmonious Music Office and the chief musician and related posts were abolished.

sentences.zh: 乾隆七年，設樂部，簡典樂大臣領之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qianlong the Music Directorate was established, with a director of music specially selected to head it.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 7 the Music Directorate was established under a specially chosen director of music.

sentences.zh: 置和聲署官，以內府、太常、鴻臚各官兼攝，侍從、待詔為加銜。

translations.literal: Harmonious Sounds Office posts were established, filled concurrently by officials of the Imperial Household, Taichang, and Honglu; attendant and awaiting-edict titles were added brevets.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonious Sounds Office posts were filled concurrently by imperial household, Taichang, and Honglu officials, with attendant and awaiting-edict titles as added brevets.

sentences.zh: 並詔禁太常樂員習道教，不原改業者削籍。

translations.literal: An edict also forbade Taichang musicians to practice Daoism; those unwilling to change profession were struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also forbade Taichang musicians to practice Daoism; those who would not change profession were struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 先是依明制，凡樂官祀丞概用道流。

translations.literal: Earlier, following the Ming system, music officers and sacrificial assistants were generally drawn from Daoist clergy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, following Ming practice, music officers and sacrificial assistants were generally Daoist clergy.

sentences.zh: 明年，改神樂觀為所，知觀為知所。

translations.literal: The following year the Divine Music Observatory was renamed an office, and the observatory director became office director.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Divine Music Observatory became an office and its director an office director.

sentences.zh: 十三年，復改神樂所為署，更提點曰署正，知所曰署丞。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year it was again changed from the Divine Music Office to the Divine Music Directorate; the intendant was renamed director and the office director deputy director.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Divine Music Office became the Divine Music Directorate, the intendant was renamed director, and the office director deputy director.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書，左、右侍郎，俱滿、漢一人。

translations.literal: Minister of War and left and right vice ministers—one Manchu and one Han each.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of War and left and right vice ministers each had one Manchu and one Han appointee.

sentences.zh: 其屬：堂主事，清檔房滿洲二人，漢本房滿洲二人，漢軍一人。

translations.literal: Subordinates: hall secretaries—the Manchu archive office two Manchus; the Han memorial office two Manchus and one Han Bannerman.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates included hall secretaries: two Manchus in the Manchu archive office; in the Han memorial office two Manchus and one Han Bannerman.

sentences.zh: 司務□司務，滿、漢各一人。

translations.literal: Registry managers (□), one Manchu and one Han each.
translations.idiomatic: Registry managers (□), one Manchu and one Han each.

sentences.zh: 繕本筆帖式十有五人。

translations.literal: Fifteen copy clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen copy clerks served.

sentences.zh: 武選、車駕、職方、武庫四清吏司：郎中，宗室一人，車駕司置。

translations.literal: Nineteen Han Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteen Han Chinese.

sentences.zh: 湖廣、陝西司各二人，餘俱一人。

translations.literal: Two each for the Huguang and Shaanxi secretariats, one each for the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang and Shaanxi had two each; the rest had one each.

sentences.zh: 員外郎，宗室二人，廣東、雲南司各一人。

translations.literal: Vice directors: two imperial clansmen; one each for the Guangdong and Yunnan bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Vice directors included two imperial clansmen and one each for the Guangdong and Yunnan bureaus.

sentences.zh: 滿洲二十有三人，江蘇、湖廣、河南、山東、陝西、廣東司各二人，餘俱一人。

translations.literal: Twenty-three Manchus; two each for the Jiangsu, Huguang, Henan, Shandong, Shaanxi, and Guangdong bureaus; one for all others.
translations.idiomatic: There were twenty-three Manchu vice directors: two each for Jiangsu, Huguang, Henan, Shandong, Shaanxi, and Guangdong, and one for every other bureau.

sentences.zh: 蒙古一人，直隸司置。

translations.literal: One Mongol, post in the Zhili Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: One Mongol post, assigned to the Zhili Bureau.

sentences.zh: 漢十有九人。

translations.literal: Nineteen Han Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteen Han Chinese vice directors.

sentences.zh: 直隸、浙江司二人，餘俱一人。

translations.literal: Two each for the Zhili and Zhejiang bureaus; one for all others.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhili and Zhejiang bureaus had two each; all other bureaus had one.

sentences.zh: 主事，宗室一人，廣西司置。

translations.literal: Secretaries: one imperial clansman, post in the Guangxi Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: One clansman served as secretary in the Guangxi Bureau.

sentences.zh: 滿洲十有五人，除奉天、湖廣二司外，司各一人。

translations.literal: Fifteen Manchus; except for the Fengtian and Huguang bureaus, one per bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen Manchu secretaries: one per bureau except Fengtian and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 蒙古一人，山西司置。

translations.literal: One Mongol, post in the Shanxi Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: One Mongol secretary, assigned to the Shanxi Bureau.

sentences.zh: 漢十有七人。

translations.literal: Seventeen Han Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen Han Chinese secretaries.

sentences.zh: 司各一人。

translations.literal: One per bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Each bureau had one secretary.

sentences.zh: 督捕清吏司：郎中，滿、漢各一人。

translations.literal: Bureau for Pursuit and Arrest: directors, one Manchu and one Han each.
translations.idiomatic: The Pursuit and Arrest Bureau had one Manchu and one Han director.

sentences.zh: 員外郎，滿洲一人。

translations.literal: Vice director: one Manchu.
translations.idiomatic: One Manchu vice director.

sentences.zh: 主事，滿、漢各一人。

translations.literal: Secretary: one Manchu and one Han each.
translations.idiomatic: One Manchu and one Han secretary.

sentences.zh: 筆帖式，宗室一人，滿洲百有三人，蒙古四人，漢軍十有五人。

translations.literal: Clerks: one imperial clansman; 103 Manchus; four Mongols; fifteen Han Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks included one clansman, 103 Manchus, four Mongols, and fifteen Han Banner men.

sentences.zh: 提牢□主事，滿、漢各一人。

translations.literal: Detention (□) director secretary, one Manchu and one Han each.
translations.idiomatic: The detention directorate (□) had one Manchu and one Han secretary.

sentences.zh: 由額外及試俸主事引見補授。

translations.literal: Filled through presentation and appointment from supernumerary and probationary secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Posts were filled by presenting supernumerary and probationary secretaries for appointment.

sentences.zh: 司獄，從九品。

translations.literal: Prison warden, subordinate ninth grade.
translations.idiomatic: Prison wardens ranked subordinate ninth grade.

sentences.zh: 滿洲四人，漢軍、漢各一人。

translations.literal: Four Manchus; one Han Banner and one Han Chinese each.
translations.idiomatic: Four Manchu wardens, plus one Han Banner and one Han Chinese.

sentences.zh: 贓罰庫，正七品。

translations.literal: Confiscated-fines treasury, regular seventh grade.
translations.idiomatic: The confiscated-fines treasury ranked regular seventh grade.

sentences.zh: 滿洲一人。

translations.literal: One Manchu.
translations.idiomatic: One Manchu official.

sentences.zh: 庫使，未入流。

translations.literal: Treasury attendant, outside the regular ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Treasury attendants lay outside the regular bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 滿洲二人。

translations.literal: Two Manchus.
translations.idiomatic: Two Manchu attendants.

sentences.zh: 尚書掌折獄審刑，簡覈法律，各省讞疑，處當具報，以肅邦紀。

translations.literal: The minister adjudicated cases and reviewed punishments, examined and verified statutes, decided doubtful cases reported from the provinces, and submitted full findings to uphold national discipline.
translations.idiomatic: The minister tried cases and reviewed sentences, checked the code, ruled on doubtful provincial reports, and submitted complete findings to maintain national order.

sentences.zh: 侍郎貳之。

translations.literal: Vice ministers assisted.
translations.idiomatic: Vice ministers assisted him.

sentences.zh: 十七司各掌其分省所屬刑名。

translations.literal: The seventeen bureaus each managed penal affairs of their assigned provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the seventeen bureaus handled criminal matters for its province.

sentences.zh: 直隸司兼掌八旗遊牧、察哈爾左翼所屬，並理京畿道御史、順天府、東西陵、熱河都統、圍場總管、密雲副都統、山海關副都統、古北口、張家口、獨石口、喜峰口、蘆峰口、塔子溝、三座塔、八溝、烏蘭哈達、喀拉河屯、多倫諾爾文移。

translations.literal: The Zhili Bureau also managed Eight Banners pastoral domains and Left Chahar subjects, and handled correspondence of the metropolitan censors of the capital circuit, Shuntian Prefecture, the eastern and western imperial tombs, the Rehe commander-in-chief, the imperial hunting-grounds superintendent, the Miyun and Shanhaiguan deputy commanders, Gubeikou, Zhangjiakou, Dushikou, Xifengkou, Lufengkou, Tower Ditch, Three Pagodas, Bagou, Ulanhada, Karahoton, and Dolon Nor.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhili Bureau also oversaw Eight Banner pastures and Left Chahar subjects and handled paperwork for capital censors, Shuntian Prefecture, the eastern and western tombs, the Rehe commander, the hunt-grounds superintendent, Miyun and Shanhaiguan deputies, and the frontier passes from Gubeikou through Dolon Nor.

sentences.zh: 奉天司兼掌吉林、黑龍江所屬，並理宗人府、理籓院文移。

translations.literal: The Fengtian Bureau also managed Jilin and Heilongjiang subjects and handled correspondence of the Court of the Imperial Clan and the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Fengtian Bureau also covered Jilin and Heilongjiang and handled documents for the Imperial Clan Court and the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 江蘇司兼掌各省減免之案，凡遇恩赦，審詳具奏。

translations.literal: The Jiangsu Bureau also managed provincial commutation and remission cases; whenever an amnesty occurred, it examined details and memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangsu Bureau also handled provincial remission cases and, at each amnesty, reviewed and memorialized them in full.

sentences.zh: 並理江南道御史、江寧將軍、京口副都統、漕運總督、南河總督文移。

translations.literal: It also handled correspondence of the Jiangnan circuit censors, the Jiangning general, the Jingkou deputy commander, the Director-General of Grain Transport, and the Southern Rivers director-general.
translations.idiomatic: It also handled paperwork for Jiangnan censors, the Jiangning general, the Jingkou deputy commander, and the grain-transport and Southern Rivers directors-general.

sentences.zh: 安徽司兼理鑲紅旗、宣武門文移。

translations.literal: The Anhui Bureau also handled correspondence of the Bordered Red Banner and Xuanwu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Anhui Bureau also handled Bordered Red Banner and Xuanwu Gate correspondence.

sentences.zh: 江西司兼理江西道御史、中城御史、正黃旗、西直門文移。

translations.literal: The Jiangxi Bureau also handled correspondence of the Jiangxi circuit censors, the central-city censors, the Bordered Yellow Banner, and Xizhi Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangxi Bureau also handled Jiangxi circuit censors, central-city censors, the Bordered Yellow Banner, and Xizhi Gate.

sentences.zh: 浙江司兼理都察院刑科、浙江道御史、南城御史、杭州將軍、乍浦副都統文移。

translations.literal: The Zhejiang Bureau also handled correspondence of the Censorate penal section, Zhejiang circuit censors, southern-city censors, the Hangzhou general, and the Zhapu deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhejiang Bureau also handled Censorate penal affairs, Zhejiang and southern-city censors, the Hangzhou general, and the Zhapu deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 並司條奏匯題，及各司爰書駁正者，會其成，比年一奏。

translations.literal: It also managed compilation and joint memorial of regulatory submissions, and when bureaus corrected case reports it convened the finished texts and memorialized annually.
translations.idiomatic: It also compiled joint regulatory memorials and, when bureaus revised case reports, assembled the final versions for an annual memorial.

sentences.zh: 福建司兼理都察院戶科、倉場衙門、左右兩翼監督、鑲藍旗、阜成門、福州將軍文移。

translations.literal: The Fujian Bureau also handled correspondence of the Censorate revenue section, granary offices, left- and right-wing supervisors, the Bordered Blue Banner, Fucheng Gate, and the Fuzhou general.
translations.idiomatic: The Fujian Bureau also handled Censorate revenue affairs, granary offices, wing supervisors, the Bordered Blue Banner, Fucheng Gate, and the Fuzhou general.

sentences.zh: 湖廣司兼掌湖北、湖南所屬，並理湖廣道御史、荊州將軍文移。

translations.literal: The Huguang Bureau also managed Hubei and Hunan subjects and handled correspondence of Huguang circuit censors and the Jingzhou general.
translations.idiomatic: The Huguang Bureau also covered Hubei and Hunan and handled Huguang censors and the Jingzhou general.

sentences.zh: 河南司兼理禮部、都察院禮科、河南道御史、太常寺、光祿寺、國子監、鴻臚寺、欽天監、太醫院、東城御史、正紅旗、德勝門文移。

translations.literal: The Henan Bureau also handled correspondence of the Ministry of Rites, the Censorate rites section, Henan circuit censors, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Court of Imperial Entertainments, Directorate of Education, Court of State Ceremonial, Directorate of Astronomy, Imperial Medical Academy, eastern-city censors, the Plain Red Banner, and Desheng Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan Bureau also handled Rites Ministry and Censorate rites business, Henan censors, ritual and education agencies, the astronomical and medical directorates, eastern-city censors, the Plain Red Banner, and Desheng Gate.

sentences.zh: 凡夏令熱審，頒行各省欽恤如制。

translations.literal: Each summer it conducted the hot-weather assize and issued provincial clemency according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In summer it ran the hot-weather assize and issued provincial clemency as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 山東司兼理兵部、都察院兵科、山東道御史、太僕寺、青州副都統、東河總督文移。

translations.literal: The Shandong Bureau also handled correspondence of the Ministry of War, the Censorate military section, Shandong circuit censors, the Court of the Imperial Stud, the Qingzhou deputy commander, and the Eastern Rivers director-general.
translations.idiomatic: The Shandong Bureau also handled War Ministry and military-censor business, Shandong censors, the Imperial Stud, the Qingzhou deputy commander, and the Eastern Rivers director-general.

sentences.zh: 凡步軍營捕獲盜賊，歲登其數請敘。

translations.literal: When the metropolitan gendarmerie captured bandits, it yearly registered the count and memorialized for rewards of service.
translations.idiomatic: Each year it recorded bandits captured by the metropolitan gendarmerie and memorialized for service rewards.

sentences.zh: 山西司兼理察哈爾右翼、綏遠城將軍、歸化城副都統、定邊左副將軍、科布多參贊大臣、庫倫辦事大臣所屬，並理軍機處、內閣、翰林院、詹事府、起居注、中書科、內廷各館、內務府、山西道御史、北城御史、鑲白旗、崇文門文移，及各省年例咨報之案。

translations.literal: The Shanxi Bureau also handled correspondence of Right Chahar, the Suiyuan general, the Guihuacheng deputy commander, the Dingbian left vice commander, the Kobdo consultant, the Urga resident minister, the Grand Council, Grand Secretariat, Hanlin Academy, Court of the Heir Apparent, Imperial Diary Office, Secretariat of the Palace Secretariat, inner-court libraries, Imperial Household, Shanxi circuit censors, northern-city censors, the Bordered White Banner, Chongwen Gate, and annual reports from all provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanxi Bureau also handled Right Chahar, northwest garrisons, central agencies from the Grand Council through the Imperial Household, Shanxi and northern-city censors, the Bordered White Banner, Chongwen Gate, and provinces' annual reports.

sentences.zh: 陝西司兼掌甘肅、伊犁、烏魯木齊、塔爾巴哈台、葉爾羌、喀什噶爾、烏什、阿克蘇、庫車、吐魯番、哈喇沙爾、和闐、哈密所屬，並理陝西道御史、大理寺、西城御史、西安將軍、寧夏將軍、涼州副都統、伊犁將軍文移。

translations.literal: The Shaanxi Bureau also managed Gansu, Ili, Urumqi, Tarbagatai, Yarkand, Kashgar, Ush, Aksu, Kucha, Turfan, Karashahr, Khotan, and Hami subjects, and handled correspondence of Shaanxi circuit censors, the Court of Revision, western-city censors, and the Xi'an, Ningxia, and Liangzhou generals and the Ili general.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaanxi Bureau also covered Gansu and the Xinjiang posts and handled Shaanxi and western-city censors, the Court of Revision, and generals at Xi'an, Ningxia, Liangzhou, and Ili.

sentences.zh: 囚糧則以時散給。

translations.literal: Prisoners' grain rations were disbursed on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Prison grain was issued on schedule.

sentences.zh: 四川司兼理工部、都察院工科、四川道御史、成都將軍文移。

translations.literal: The Sichuan Bureau also handled correspondence of the Ministry of Works, the Censorate works section, Sichuan circuit censors, and the Chengdu general.
translations.idiomatic: The Sichuan Bureau also handled Works Ministry and works-censor business, Sichuan censors, and the Chengdu general.

sentences.zh: 凡秋審，會九卿、詹事於朝房以定爰書，並收發刑具。

translations.literal: For the autumn assize, it convened the nine ministers and chancellors of the heir apparent in the morning hall to fix case reports, and also received and issued penal implements.
translations.idiomatic: At the autumn assize it convened ministers and heir-apparent chancellors in the morning hall to finalize case reports and managed penal equipment.

sentences.zh: 廣東司兼理鑾輿衛、正白旗、廣東道御史、安定門，廣州將軍文移。

translations.literal: The Guangdong Bureau also handled correspondence of the Imperial Carriage Guard, the Plain White Banner, Guangdong circuit censors, Anding Gate, and the Guangzhou general.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangdong Bureau also handled the Imperial Carriage Guard, the Plain White Banner, Guangdong censors, Anding Gate, and the Guangzhou general.

sentences.zh: 廣西司兼理通政司、廣西道御史文移。

translations.literal: The Guangxi Bureau also handled correspondence of the Office of Transmission and Guangxi circuit censors.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangxi Bureau also handled the Office of Transmission and Guangxi censors.

sentences.zh: 凡朝審，具題稿，囚衣則以時散給。

translations.literal: For the court assize, it prepared memorial drafts; prisoners' clothing was disbursed on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: At the court assize it drafted memorials and issued prisoners' clothing on schedule.

sentences.zh: 雲南司兼理鑲黃旗、雲南道御史，東直門文移。

translations.literal: The Yunnan Bureau also handled correspondence of the Bordered Yellow Banner, Yunnan circuit censors, and Dongzhi Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Yunnan Bureau also handled the Bordered Yellow Banner, Yunnan censors, and Dongzhi Gate.

sentences.zh: 並司堂印封啟。

translations.literal: It also managed sealing and opening of the ministry seal.
translations.idiomatic: It also sealed and opened the ministry's official seal.

sentences.zh: 貴州司兼理吏部、都察院吏科、正藍旗、貴州道御史、朝陽門文移。

translations.literal: The Guizhou Bureau also handled correspondence of the Ministry of Personnel, the Censorate personnel section, the Plain Blue Banner, Guizhou circuit censors, and Chaoyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The Guizhou Bureau also handled Personnel Ministry and personnel-censor business, the Plain Blue Banner, Guizhou censors, and Chaoyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 並定各司漢員升補。

translations.literal: It also fixed promotions and replacements of Han officials in each bureau.
translations.idiomatic: It also regulated Han promotions and replacements across the bureaus.

sentences.zh: 督捕司掌八旗及各省逃亡。

translations.literal: The Pursuit Bureau managed fugitives of the Eight Banners and all provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The Pursuit Bureau tracked fugitives in the Eight Banners and every province.

sentences.zh: 提牢□掌檢獄圄。

translations.literal: The detention directorate (□) supervised inspection of prisons.
translations.idiomatic: The detention office (□) inspected the prisons.

sentences.zh: 司獄掌督獄卒。

translations.literal: Prison wardens supervised jailers.
translations.idiomatic: Wardens supervised the jail staff.

sentences.zh: 贓罰庫掌貯現審贓款，會數送戶部。

translations.literal: The confiscated-fines treasury stored funds from on-trial cases and periodically sent the sums to the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The confiscated-fines treasury held trial forfeitures and periodically remitted them to the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 別設律例館，由尚書或侍郎充總裁。

translations.literal: A separate Statutes Office was established, with the minister or vice minister serving as chief compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A Statutes Office was set apart, headed by the minister or a vice minister as chief compiler.

sentences.zh: 提調一人，纂修四人，司員兼充。

translations.literal: One coordinator, four compilers, filled concurrently by section officials.
translations.idiomatic: One coordinator and four compilers, drawn from section officials serving concurrently.

sentences.zh: 校對四人，收掌二人，翻譯、謄錄各四人。

translations.literal: Four proofreaders, two registrars, and four translators and four copyists each.
translations.idiomatic: Four proofreaders, two registrars, four translators, and four copyists.

sentences.zh: 司員及筆帖式充。

translations.literal: Filled by section officials and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Section officials and clerks filled these posts.

sentences.zh: 掌修條例。

translations.literal: It compiled statutory articles.
translations.idiomatic: It maintained the code articles.

sentences.zh: 五年匯輯為小修，十年重編為大修。

translations.literal: Every five years the compilation was a minor revision; every ten years a major recodification.
translations.idiomatic: Compilation every five years counted as a minor revision; every ten years as a major one.

sentences.zh: 秋審處，主覈秋錄大典。

translations.literal: The autumn-assize office directed the autumn-register compilation.
translations.idiomatic: The autumn-assize office oversaw the autumn legal register.

sentences.zh: 初以四川、廣西二司分理。

translations.literal: At first the Sichuan and Guangxi bureaus divided the work.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the Sichuan and Guangxi bureaus shared the duties.

sentences.zh: 雍正十二年，始別遣滿、漢司員各二人，曰總辦秋審處。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yongzheng, two Manchu and two Han section officials were specially dispatched, titled the General Office for Autumn Assize.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 12 two Manchu and two Han section officials were separately assigned to the General Office for Autumn Assize.

sentences.zh: 尋佐以協辦者四人。

translations.literal: Soon four associate coordinators were added.
translations.idiomatic: Four associate coordinators were soon added.

sentences.zh: 錄各省囚，謂之秋審；

translations.literal: Recording prisoners from the provinces was called the autumn assize;
translations.idiomatic: Review of provincial prisoners was called the autumn assize;

sentences.zh: 錄本部囚，謂之朝審。

translations.literal: recording prisoners of the ministry was called the court assize.
translations.idiomatic: review of the ministry's own prisoners was called the court assize.

sentences.zh: 歲八月，會九卿、詹事、科道公閱爰書，覈定情實。

translations.literal: Each year in the eighth month, ministers, heir-apparent chancellors, and censors jointly reviewed case reports in public session and verified the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Every eighth month ministers, chancellors, and censors jointly reviewed case reports and verified the facts.

sentences.zh: 凡大辟，御史、大理寺官會刑司錄問，案法隨科，曰會小三法司。

translations.literal: For capital cases, censors and Court of Revision officials joined ministry officials to record interrogations; punishment followed the code section—called joint review of the lesser Three Judicial Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Capital cases brought censors and revision officials together with ministry staff to record interrogations and apply the statute—the lesser joint review of the Three Judicial Offices.

sentences.zh: 錄畢，白長官。

translations.literal: When recording was complete, the supervising official was informed.
translations.idiomatic: When the record was finished, the chief was notified.

sentences.zh: 都御史、大理卿詣部偕尚書、侍郎會鞫，各麗法議獄，曰會大三法司。

translations.literal: The censor-in-chief and Court of Revision president came to the ministry with the minister and vice ministers for joint inquest; each applied the code to debate the case—called joint review of the greater Three Judicial Offices.
translations.idiomatic: The censor-in-chief and revision president joined the minister and vice ministers at the ministry to debate the case under the code—the greater joint review of the Three Judicial Offices.

sentences.zh: 讞上，復召大臣按覆，然後麗之於辟。

translations.literal: After the verdict was submitted upward, grand ministers were again summoned to review, and only then was the death penalty confirmed.
translations.idiomatic: Once the finding went up, senior ministers reviewed it again before the death sentence was fixed.

sentences.zh: 初制，刑部會擬朝審，俱本部案件。

translations.literal: Under the original system, the ministry's joint draft of the court assize covered only cases of the ministry itself.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the ministry's court-assize draft covered only its own prisoners.

sentences.zh: 其外省之案，康熙十六年始命刑部覆覈，九卿會議。

translations.literal: For cases from outside provinces, in the sixteenth year of Kangxi the ministry was first ordered to reexamine them with joint deliberation by the nine ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial cases were first sent back for ministry reexamination and nine-minister deliberation in Kangxi 16.

sentences.zh: 初，天聰五年，設刑部。

translations.literal: At first, in the fifth year of Tiancong, the Ministry of Justice was established.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice was first established in Tiancong 5.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，置尚書、侍郎各官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, ministers and vice ministers were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi 1 established the minister and vice minister posts.

sentences.zh: 設江南、浙江、福建、四川、湖廣、陝西、河南、江西、山東、山西、廣東、廣西、雲南、貴州十四司，置滿洲郎中六人，五年增八人。

translations.literal: Fourteen bureaus were set up—Jiangnan, Zhejiang, Fujian, Sichuan, Huguang, Shaanxi, Henan, Jiangxi, Shandong, Shanxi, Guangdong, Guangxi, Yunnan, and Guizhou—with six Manchu directors, increased to eight in the fifth year.

translations.idiomatic: In year 15 one secretary was cut from each of Henan, Sichuan, Shaanxi, and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 雍正三年復故。

translations.idiomatic: One Manchu custodian and four Han wardens.

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year of Kangxi four Manchu posts were added.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 51 added four Manchu wardens.

sentences.zh: 乾隆六年定漢軍、漢各二人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qianlong, fixed at two Han Banner and two Han Chinese each.

translations.idiomatic: Year 5 fixed one Manchu and one Han minister each.

sentences.zh: 七年增滿洲一人，十年省。

translations.literal: In the seventh year one Manchu post was added; cut in the tenth year.
translations.idiomatic: Year 7 added one Manchu minister; year 10 cut it.

sentences.zh: 十八年，置蒙古員外郎八人。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, eight Mongol vice directors were established.
translations.idiomatic: Year 18 created eight Mongol vice directors.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年省。

translations.literal: Cut in the first year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished in Kangxi 1.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十八年，增設督捕前、後司，為十六司。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Kangxi, front and rear Pursuit bureaus were added, making sixteen bureaus in all.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 38 added front and rear Pursuit bureaus for sixteen bureaus total.

sentences.zh: 由兵部並入。

translations.literal: Incorporated from the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: They were absorbed from the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，增置蒙古郎中、員外郎、主事各一人。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year, one Mongol director, vice director, and secretary each were added.
translations.idiomatic: Year 57 added one Mongol director, vice director, and secretary.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，設現審左、右二司，主鞫訊囚系。

translations.idiomatic: Yongzheng 1 created Left and Right On-trial bureaus to interrogate prisoners.

sentences.zh: 十二年，析江南司為江蘇、安徽二司，定滿、漢郎中俱各一人，滿洲員外郎三人，江蘇司二人，安徽司一人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the Jiangnan Section was split into Jiangsu and Anhui sections; Manchu and Han directors were fixed at one each; three Manchu vice directors—two for the Jiangsu Section, one for the Anhui Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the Jiangnan Section was divided into Jiangsu and Anhui sections, with one Manchu and one Han director each and three Manchu vice directors—two for Jiangsu and one for Anhui.

sentences.zh: 漢員外郎二人，滿、漢主事司各一人，並督捕前、後司為一。

translations.literal: Two Han vice directors; one Manchu and one Han section secretary each; and the front and rear Pursuit sections were merged into one.
translations.idiomatic: There were two Han vice directors and one Manchu and one Han section secretary each, and the front and rear Pursuit sections were combined.

sentences.zh: 自時厥後，親王、郡王奉命管部，無常員。

translations.literal: From then on, princes and commandery princes were ordered to administer the ministry, with no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter princes and commandery princes were ordered to run the ministry, with no fixed posts.

translations.idiomatic: A Mongol post was added to the Fengtian Section.
